No washout needed — give Sustenna in place of the next scheduled Consta dose, using deltoid loading protocol. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Inject Invega Sustenna 150 mg deltoid (loading dose 1) in place of the next scheduled Consta. Do NOT give Consta on this day.
Inject Invega Sustenna 100 mg deltoid (loading dose 2). Consta tail still releasing — combined exposure is acceptable because it's the same molecule.
First maintenance Sustenna 75 mg gluteal (or deltoid). Continue monthly. Consta has cleared.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: Consta 25 mg every 2 weeks ≈ Sustenna 75 mg monthly (Maudsley 14th). For higher Consta doses (37.5, 50 mg), use Sustenna 100 or 150 mg maintenance. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-lai-to-risperidone.rationale: Switching from Risperdal Consta (risperidone microspheres LAI) to oral risperidone. Consta has a t½ of ~3–6 weeks after the last injection. Start oral risperidone when the next Consta injection would have been due; the depot provides a natural taper. Oral risperidone and its active metabolite paliperidone (9-OH-risperidone) continue the pharmacological effect. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Skip the next scheduled Consta injection. Start oral risperidone 2 mg. Consta continues releasing — monitor for combined effect. Titrate oral if needed.
Increase oral risperidone to 3 mg. Consta level still measurable. Monitor EPS and prolactin.
Consta level declining. Oral risperidone 4 mg — approximately equivalent maintenance target.
Consta substantially cleared (~6 weeks post-last-injection). Oral monotherapy.
Consta cleared. Oral risperidone 4 mg as monotherapy. Adjust 2–8 mg based on clinical response.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Risperdal Consta 25 mg every 2 weeks ≈ oral risperidone 4 mg/day (approximate; Maudsley 15th). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

safetyFlags.title: Prolactinaemia
safetyFlags.body: Risperidone causes sustained prolactin elevation — monitor prolactin at baseline and 3 months. Consider switching to a prolactin-sparing agent if symptomatic.

safetyFlags.title: Consta depot tail
safetyFlags.body: Risperdal Consta t½ ~3–6 weeks after the last injection. Combined oral + depot levels may be elevated for the first 4–6 weeks.

risperidone-to-amisulpride.rationale: Risperidone (D2/D3 + 5-HT2A + α1/α2 + H1; moderate anticholinergic activity) to amisulpride (selective D2/D3). Both drugs are high-potency D2 antagonists that elevate prolactin significantly. Common reasons: cost or formulary (amisulpride may be cheaper), desire for a drug without H1 antihistamine sedation, or negative symptom targeting at low doses (amisulpride 50–300 mg). Risperidone has less anticholinergic activity than olanzapine/quetiapine, so cross-taper can proceed at a moderate pace. Both drugs prolong QTc — ECG monitoring during the overlap period is important. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start amisulpride 200 mg. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Baseline ECG (both drugs prolong QTc). Check renal function.
Increase amisulpride to 400 mg (target). Plateau risperidone. Monitor for additive QTc prolongation — check serum potassium if patient on diuretics or has risk factors.
Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. Amisulpride at target. Prolactin: additive elevation during overlap — if symptomatic (amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea), expedite risperidone withdrawal.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Clinical stability maintained by amisulpride at therapeutic dose.
Stop risperidone. Continue amisulpride 400 mg. Repeat ECG at 4–6 weeks. Prolactin remains elevated on amisulpride — check if this was the reason for the switch.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Risperidone 4 mg ≈ amisulpride 400 mg (Leucht et al. CMD method, Schizophrenia Bulletin 2015). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-aripiprazole-lai.rationale: Switching from oral risperidone to aripiprazole LAI (Abilify Maintena) — typically motivated by adherence concerns and the desire to escape risperidone's high prolactin burden. Aripiprazole LAI requires a mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap after the first injection. Cross-taper: the oral aripiprazole overlap runs concurrently with risperidone continuation; once the overlap is complete and the depot is therapeutic, risperidone is tapered to zero over 2 weeks. Prolactin will normalise over weeks to months after risperidone is stopped — counsel patients with established hyperprolactinaemia symptoms (amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea, sexual dysfunction) to expect resolution. Akathisia risk from aripiprazole is moderate when coming from risperidone — the D2 receptor density is moderately elevated but not as saturated as with olanzapine or quetiapine. Monitor closely in the first 2–4 weeks post-switch. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Administer Abilify Maintena 400 mg IM (deltoid or gluteal). Start oral aripiprazole 10 mg/day — 14-day oral overlap MANDATORY. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Warn patient about akathisia. Check baseline prolactin if not already documented.

Day 7: Continue oral aripiprazole 10 mg + risperidone 4 mg. Depot reaching therapeutic levels. Assess akathisia. EPS risk: aripiprazole adds moderate EPS on top of risperidone — anticholinergic cover if needed.
STOP oral aripiprazole (14-day overlap complete). Depot now therapeutic. Taper risperidone to 2 mg. Prolactin begins normalising — patients may notice symptom improvement within weeks.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Depot providing full antipsychotic cover. Continue EPS/akathisia monitoring.
Stop risperidone. Second Maintena injection due today (400 mg). Monthly thereafter. Prolactin recheck at 3 months if baseline was elevated.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: risperidone 4 mg/day ≈ aripiprazole LAI 400 mg/4 weeks (Maudsley 15th, AP dose-equivalence table + LAI conversion). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-aripiprazole.rationale: Frequent prolactin-driven or sexual-dysfunction-driven switch. Plateau cross-taper because risperidone's full D2 antagonism interacts with aripiprazole's partial agonism — abrupt aripiprazole introduction can produce paradoxical worsening or akathisia. Slow risperidone reduction after aripiprazole stabilisation. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start aripiprazole 5 mg in the morning. Hold risperidone 4 mg.
Increase aripiprazole to 10 mg. Hold risperidone. Watch for akathisia.
Increase aripiprazole to 15 mg target. Reduce risperidone to 3 mg.
Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. Hold aripiprazole.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Prolactin should already be falling — counsel about possible return of menses.
Stop risperidone. Continue aripiprazole 15 mg.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: risperidone 4 mg ≈ aripiprazole 15 mg (Maudsley 14th). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-haloperidol.rationale: SGA-to-FGA switch — cost-driven or for high D2 occupancy requirements beyond the SGA range. Both risperidone and haloperidol are potent D2 antagonists with significant EPS risk; the pharmacological step is smaller than from olanzapine or quetiapine. Prolactin remains high throughout (both agents are prolactin-raising). Key concern is the shift in QTc risk: risperidone has low QTc risk while haloperidol is high — baseline ECG before starting haloperidol. EPS burden may worsen at equivalent doses as haloperidol is the more EPS-prone agent. Anticholinergic co-prescription review: if the patient is already on benzhexol for risperidone-related EPS, continue it; if not, have a low threshold to start once haloperidol is dominant. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start haloperidol 2 mg. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Baseline ECG mandatory. Assess EPS carefully at each visit.
Increase haloperidol to 5 mg target. Plateau risperidone — allow haloperidol to stabilise before tapering.
Begin tapering risperidone to 3 mg. Monitor for EPS worsening as haloperidol becomes the dominant AP.
Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. Prescribe benzhexol if EPS emerging. Recheck QTc — haloperidol's QTc contribution now significant.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Haloperidol providing primary antipsychotic cover.
Stop risperidone. Continue haloperidol 5 mg. Document metabolic baseline — expect improvement. Consider depot (haloperidol decanoate) if adherence is a concern.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: risperidone 4 mg ≈ haloperidol 5 mg (Maudsley 15th, AP dose-equivalence table). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-lurasidone.rationale: Risperidone (D2/D3 + 5-HT2A + α1/α2 + H1; prolactin elevation; moderate QTc) to lurasidone (D2, 5-HT2A, 5-HT7, 5-HT1A partial agonist; lower prolactin elevation; low QTc risk; food-dependent). Common reasons: prolactin-related side effects, QTc concerns, or seeking better tolerability. Prolactin will decrease on lurasidone. QTc risk diminishes. Lurasidone's food requirement must be explicitly taught. Risperidone has minimal anticholinergic activity so cross-taper can proceed at a standard pace without significant cholinergic rebound. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start lurasidone 40 mg with main meal. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Counsel patient: lurasidone must be taken with ≥350 kcal — food is essential for adequate absorption.
Increase lurasidone to 80 mg. Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. Prolactin beginning to fall as risperidone is reduced.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Lurasidone at target dose. Clinical stability should be maintained.
Stop risperidone. Continue lurasidone 80 mg. Prolactin levels should normalise over 2–4 weeks. Counsel female patients about possible menstrual cycle changes.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Risperidone 4 mg ≈ lurasidone 80 mg (inferred from DDD equivalence; both ≈ olanzapine 10 mg by proxy). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-olanzapine.rationale: Typically an EPS-driven switch — risperidone's moderate EPS burden (especially above 4 mg) prompts a move to olanzapine's lower EPS profile. Introduce olanzapine first and stabilise at target before tapering risperidone, to avoid a window of sub-therapeutic cover. Counsel the patient that metabolic risk increases with olanzapine — weight, glucose and lipid monitoring is mandatory. Cholinergic and histaminergic effects of olanzapine will produce sedation initially; dose at night. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start olanzapine 5 mg nocte. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Warn patient about initial sedation and weight gain trajectory.
Increase olanzapine to 10 mg nocte (target dose). Hold risperidone 4 mg — allow olanzapine to stabilise before tapering.
Begin tapering risperidone: reduce to 3 mg. Olanzapine at steady state, antipsychotic cover maintained.
Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. Prolactin will begin to normalise as risperidone withdraws — counsel accordingly.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Watch for any emergence of psychotic symptoms at this low dose.
Stop risperidone. Continue olanzapine 10 mg. Establish baseline weight, fasting glucose and lipids if not done at switch initiation.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: risperidone 4 mg ≈ olanzapine 10 mg (Maudsley 15th, AP dose-equivalence table). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-paliperidone-lai.rationale: Pharmacologically the smoothest oral-to-LAI transition in the registry: paliperidone IS the 9-OH-risperidone active metabolite of oral risperidone, so patients are already tolerant of the active molecule. Switching from risperidone oral to paliperidone palmitate LAI provides the adherence benefits of a monthly depot with no pharmacological novelty risk. Paliperidone's loading protocol (150 mg deltoid day 1, 100 mg deltoid day 8) removes the need for an oral paliperidone run-in. Oral risperidone is tapered during loading — there is no therapeutic gap. Prolactin remains high (both agents are prolactin-raising) — no change expected. Clinical equivalency is well-established. No separate oral paliperidone bridge required. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Give Invega Sustenna 150 mg deltoid (loading dose 1). Continue oral risperidone 4 mg. Patient is already tolerant of the active molecule (paliperidone). Counsel: 2 loading injections, then monthly maintenance.
Invega Sustenna 100 mg deltoid (loading dose 2, day 8 ± 2 days). Continue oral risperidone 4 mg. PP-LAI building — combined risperidone + paliperidone exposure is the same active molecule.
PP-LAI now at therapeutic maintenance levels. Halve oral risperidone to 2 mg. Total active drug exposure unchanged.
Stop oral risperidone. First maintenance Sustenna injection (100 mg; deltoid or gluteal). Monthly thereafter.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Established clinical equivalency: oral risperidone 4 mg/day ≈ paliperidone palmitate 100 mg/4 weeks. Paliperidone is risperidone's active metabolite (9-OH-risperidone) — conversion is direct. For risperidone 2 mg/day, use Sustenna 75 mg. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-quetiapine.rationale: EPS-driven switch, or patient preference for a more sedating agent (sleep benefit, anxiety). Quetiapine's lower D2 occupancy and strong H1/α1 blockade profile will introduce sedation and improve sleep quickly once doses exceed 50–100 mg. Prolactin will normalise progressively as risperidone withdraws. Cross-taper is preferred over abrupt switch because quetiapine's antihistaminergic cover fills in as risperidone's antipsychotic effect is withdrawn. Warn patient on metabolic monitoring — quetiapine has significant weight gain liability above 300 mg. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start quetiapine 50 mg nocte. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Sedation expected — advise driving caution.
Increase quetiapine to 100 mg. Begin reducing risperidone to 3 mg.
Increase quetiapine to 200 mg. Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. EPS should be improving.
Quetiapine at 300 mg target. Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Monitor for rebound insomnia — quetiapine's histaminergic cover now dominant.
Stop risperidone. Continue quetiapine 300 mg. Check weight and fasting glucose at switch completion.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: risperidone 4 mg ≈ quetiapine 300 mg (Maudsley 15th, AP dose-equivalence table). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

risperidone-to-risperidone-lai.rationale: Standard oral-to-LAI initiation: confirm tolerability of oral risperidone first, then start Risperdal Consta with mandatory 21-day oral overlap because the microsphere depot does not reach therapeutic levels until ~3 weeks after the first injection. Stopping oral too early risks relapse during the gap. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Continue oral risperidone 4 mg. Inject Risperdal Consta 25 mg deltoid (first injection). Counsel patient that depot takes 3 weeks to start working.
Continue oral risperidone 4 mg. Second Consta 25 mg injection (every 2 weeks).
Reduce oral to 2 mg as depot begins to release. Clinical effect of Consta now emerging.
Stop oral risperidone. Third Consta 25 mg injection. Maintenance every 2 weeks ongoing.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: oral risperidone 4 mg/day ≈ Consta 25 mg every 2 weeks (Maudsley 14th). For higher oral doses (>4 mg), use Consta 37.5 or 50 mg. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sertraline-to-agomelatine.rationale: Sertraline (SSRI; t½ ~26h; moderate discontinuation syndrome risk) to agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist, 5-HT2C antagonist; t½ ~2h). Sertraline has moderate discontinuation syndrome risk — taper over at least 2 weeks. Agomelatine can be started during the sertraline taper without serotonin syndrome risk. Sertraline is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor but agomelatine is metabolised by CYP1A2 (not CYP2D6) — no interaction. CRITICAL: Baseline LFTs before starting agomelatine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Continue sertraline 100 mg. CHECK BASELINE LFTs before starting agomelatine. No serotonin syndrome risk: agomelatine does not inhibit serotonin reuptake. Sertraline is a CYP2D6 inhibitor — no interaction with agomelatine (CYP1A2 substrate).
Reduce sertraline to 50 mg. Continue agomelatine 25 mg. Monitor for discontinuation symptoms at this reduction.
Stop sertraline. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Sertraline discontinuation is usually mild — dizziness, irritability. Titrate agomelatine to 50 mg at 2 weeks if inadequate response.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sertraline 100 mg → agomelatine 25 mg (standard dose range for MDD). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

contraindications: Hepatic impairment — agomelatine contraindicated.
ALT >3× ULN at baseline — do not start agomelatine.

sertraline-to-desvenlafaxine.rationale: Sertraline (SSRI; moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor) to desvenlafaxine (SNRI; not primarily CYP2D6-metabolised). Sertraline's moderate CYP2D6 inhibition has minimal effect on desvenlafaxine levels (unlike venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine bypasses CYP2D6 metabolism to a large extent). Standard SSRI→SNRI cross-taper: start desvenlafaxine, overlap briefly, taper sertraline. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Continue sertraline 100 mg. Sertraline's moderate CYP2D6 inhibition has minimal effect on desvenlafaxine (largely non-CYP2D6 metabolised). Standard dose — no adjustment required.
Reduce sertraline to 50 mg. Continue desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Monitor for sertraline discontinuation symptoms.
Stop sertraline. Continue desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Titrate to 100 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sertraline 100 mg → desvenlafaxine 50 mg (standard effective doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sertraline-to-duloxetine.rationale: SSRI-to-SNRI switch, particularly useful when comorbid neuropathic pain or chronic musculoskeletal pain favours noradrenergic activity. Sertraline disc risk is moderate; duloxetine titrates slowly. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start duloxetine 30 mg. Hold sertraline 100 mg.
Halve sertraline to 50 mg. Increase duloxetine to 60 mg target.
Reduce sertraline to 25 mg. Hold duloxetine.
Stop sertraline. Continue duloxetine 60 mg. Counsel re duloxetine's high disc risk if later stopped.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: sertraline 100 mg ≈ duloxetine 60 mg (Maudsley 14th). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sertraline-to-escitalopram.rationale: Both drugs are SSRIs with overlapping mechanism. A graded cross-taper over ~11 days minimises both serotonin-syndrome risk on overlap and discontinuation symptoms on the sertraline side. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start escitalopram 5 mg. Halve sertraline to 50 mg from day 4.
Continue escitalopram 5 mg. Hold sertraline at 50 mg.
Reduce sertraline to 25 mg. Increase escitalopram to 10 mg target.
Stop sertraline. Continue escitalopram 10 mg.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: sertraline 50 mg ≈ escitalopram 10 mg (Maudsley 14th ed.). Equivalency is approximate and should not be used outside this reviewed pair. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sertraline-to-fluoxetine.rationale: Common reasons to switch: simplifying dosing, leveraging fluoxetine's long half-life to auto-taper, or planning a future switch where the long norfluoxetine washout is acceptable. Brief cross-taper is sufficient because fluoxetine reaches steady state slowly and sertraline is moderate-disc-risk only. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start fluoxetine 20 mg in the morning. Hold sertraline 100 mg.
Halve sertraline to 50 mg. Hold fluoxetine 20 mg.
Stop sertraline. Continue fluoxetine 20 mg. Norfluoxetine will auto-taper any residual sertraline-like effect over weeks.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: sertraline 100 mg ≈ fluoxetine 20 mg (Maudsley 14th). Note: this switch commits the patient to a multi-week wash-IN of fluoxetine and a 5-week washout requirement before any future MAOI. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sertraline-to-venlafaxine.rationale: SSRI-to-SNRI swap, often considered after non-response to a serotonergic-only agent. Brief cross-taper is sufficient because sertraline disc risk is moderate and venlafaxine titrates slowly anyway. Watch baseline blood pressure before starting venlafaxine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start venlafaxine XR 37.5 mg. Hold sertraline 100 mg. Check baseline blood pressure.
Halve sertraline to 50 mg. Increase venlafaxine XR to 75 mg.
Reduce sertraline to 25 mg. Increase venlafaxine XR to 150 mg target. Re-check blood pressure.
Stop sertraline. Continue venlafaxine XR 150 mg. Counsel re very-high disc risk if venlafaxine is later stopped.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: sertraline 100 mg ≈ venlafaxine 150 mg XR (Maudsley 14th). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sertraline-to-vortioxetine.rationale: Sertraline (SSRI; t½ ~26h; moderate CYP2D6 inhibition) to vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; CYP2D6 substrate). KEY PHARMACOKINETIC INTERACTION: Sertraline is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor — it raises vortioxetine plasma levels. During the cross-taper period when both drugs are present, vortioxetine levels may be higher than expected. Recommended approach: start vortioxetine at 10 mg (not higher) during the overlap, as sertraline's CYP2D6 inhibition will produce equivalent exposure to a higher vortioxetine dose. Only titrate vortioxetine upward after sertraline is fully stopped. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start vortioxetine 10 mg. Continue sertraline 100 mg. START VORTIOXETINE AT 10 MG — sertraline's moderate CYP2D6 inhibition raises vortioxetine levels during overlap. Do not start at higher vortioxetine dose during cross-taper.
Reduce sertraline to 50 mg. Hold vortioxetine at 10 mg. As sertraline reduces, CYP2D6 inhibition decreases — vortioxetine levels may adjust.
Stop sertraline. Continue vortioxetine 10 mg. Now sertraline CYP2D6 inhibition fully reversed — safe to titrate vortioxetine to 20 mg at 2 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sertraline 100 mg → vortioxetine 10 mg (start during cross-taper; titrate to 20 mg after sertraline stopped). CYP2D6 interaction means lower vortioxetine starting dose during overlap. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sulpiride-to-aripiprazole.rationale: Sulpiride (full D2 antagonist) to aripiprazole (partial D2/D3 agonist). Common reasons: prolactin reduction, weight neutrality, or improved tolerability. Akathisia risk on aripiprazole is significant — patients stabilised on full D2 blockade are at highest risk. Prolactin will normalise after the switch. No cholinergic rebound from sulpiride (no anticholinergic activity). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start aripiprazole 10 mg. Continue sulpiride 800 mg. Counsel patient about akathisia risk — restlessness typically peaks in first 2 weeks. Propranolol PRN can be prescribed proactively.
Increase aripiprazole to 15 mg (target). Plateau sulpiride. Review akathisia at week 1 check-in.
Reduce sulpiride to 400 mg. Aripiprazole at steady state. Insomnia may emerge as sulpiride's mild sedation is withdrawn.
Reduce sulpiride to 200 mg. Prolactin falling — counsel female patients about possible menstrual cycle restoration.
Stop sulpiride. Continue aripiprazole 15 mg. Prolactin should normalise over 2–4 weeks. No QTc concerns with aripiprazole.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sulpiride 800 mg ≈ aripiprazole 15 mg (via DDD equivalence; both ≈ olanzapine 10 mg by proxy). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sulpiride-to-olanzapine.rationale: Sulpiride (selective D2/D3 + some D4; minimal anticholinergic activity; renally excreted; high prolactin) to olanzapine (multi-receptor SGA; high metabolic risk; strong H1/M1 activity). Sulpiride is sometimes used in Malaysia for negative symptoms (low doses 200–400 mg) or as cost-effective antipsychotic. Common reason for switch: insufficient efficacy, metabolic acceptance of olanzapine for better tolerability of EPS, or formulary. Sulpiride has minimal anticholinergic activity, so cross-taper can proceed at a standard pace without significant cholinergic rebound. Metabolic monitoring is essential as metabolic risk increases significantly on olanzapine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start olanzapine 5 mg nocte. Continue sulpiride 800 mg. Record baseline weight, fasting glucose, fasting lipids before starting olanzapine.
Increase olanzapine to 10 mg nocte (target). Plateau sulpiride. Allow olanzapine to approach steady state.
Reduce sulpiride to 400 mg. Prolactin levels fall as sulpiride is reduced — warn female patients about possible menstrual changes.
Reduce sulpiride to 200 mg. Olanzapine at steady state. Sedation and weight increase likely.
Stop sulpiride. Continue olanzapine 10 mg nocte. Metabolic monitoring at 4 and 12 weeks. Dietary counselling for weight management.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sulpiride 800 mg ≈ olanzapine 10 mg (DDD-equivalence: sulpiride 800 mg/day ≈ olanzapine 10 mg/day; Maudsley 15th CPZ-equivalence: sulpiride 200 mg ≈ CPZ 100 mg ≈ olanzapine 2.5 mg). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sulpiride-to-quetiapine.rationale: Sulpiride (selective D2/D3, no sedation, high prolactin, renal excretion) to quetiapine (broad receptor profile: D2, 5-HT2A, H1, M1, α1/α2; moderate metabolic risk; antidepressant augmentation via norquetiapine). Common reasons: bipolar depression requiring mood stabilisation with quetiapine's antidepressant profile, desire for insomnia management, or reducing prolactin. Sulpiride withdrawal is generally well tolerated — no significant anticholinergic rebound. Quetiapine initiation brings sedation, postural hypotension, and metabolic risk. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start quetiapine 100 mg nocte. Continue sulpiride 800 mg. Record baseline metabolic parameters. Warn about postural hypotension on quetiapine initiation.
Increase quetiapine to 200 mg nocte. Plateau sulpiride.
Increase quetiapine to 400 mg (target). Reduce sulpiride to 400 mg. Prolactin will begin to fall as sulpiride reduces.
Reduce sulpiride to 200 mg. Quetiapine well established. Monitor metabolic parameters.
Stop sulpiride. Continue quetiapine 400 mg. Metabolic monitoring at 4 and 12 weeks.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sulpiride 800 mg ≈ quetiapine 400 mg (via DDD and CPZ equivalence proxy). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

sulpiride-to-risperidone.rationale: Sulpiride (D2/D3 selective, renally excreted, high prolactin, no anticholinergic activity) to risperidone (D2/D3 + 5-HT2A + α1/α2 + H1). Both drugs elevate prolactin significantly (no improvement expected). Both carry moderate QTc risk. The transition is relatively straightforward as both have similar D2 dominance without significant anticholinergic burden. A lateral switch within the high-D2-blockade class. Common reason: cost, formulary, or seeking risperidone LAI (paliperidone LAI). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start risperidone 2 mg. Continue sulpiride 800 mg. ECG at baseline.
Increase risperidone to 4 mg (target). Plateau sulpiride.
Reduce sulpiride to 400 mg. Additive prolactin elevation during overlap — monitor for symptoms.
Reduce sulpiride to 200 mg. Clinical stability maintained by risperidone.
Stop sulpiride. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Review for LAI transition if planned.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Sulpiride 800 mg ≈ risperidone 4 mg (via CPZ equivalence proxy: sulpiride 200 mg ≈ CPZ 100 mg ≈ risperidone 1 mg; therefore sulpiride 800 mg ≈ risperidone 4 mg). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

trifluoperazine-to-aripiprazole.rationale: Trifluoperazine (high-potency piperazine FGA; full D2 antagonist; high EPS; moderate anticholinergic activity; high prolactin; moderate QTc) to aripiprazole (partial D2/D3 agonist + 5-HT1A partial agonist; EPS rare at therapeutic doses; prolactin-sparing; minimal QTc risk). Switching from full D2 blockade to partial agonism carries significant akathisia risk — patients on stable high-D2 blockade are most vulnerable. EPS and prolactin should improve, but akathisia requires proactive management. Trifluoperazine's moderate anticholinergic activity means some cholinergic rebound is possible — aripiprazole provides no anticholinergic cover. Document baseline involuntary movements (tardive dyskinesia risk on trifluoperazine withdrawal). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start aripiprazole 10 mg. Continue trifluoperazine 10 mg. Baseline AIMS assessment. Counsel patient explicitly about akathisia — restlessness may emerge within days of aripiprazole initiation. Propranolol 10–30 mg PRN can be prescribed proactively.
Increase aripiprazole to 15 mg (target). Plateau trifluoperazine. Review akathisia at week 1. EPS from trifluoperazine still covered — transition period.
Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. Aripiprazole at steady state. Monitor for withdrawal dyskinesias — unmasking of latent tardive dyskinesia possible. Insomnia may emerge as sedating FGA effect reduces.
Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. Prolactin falling — counsel female patients about possible menstrual cycle restoration. Anticholinergic agents for EPS may now be withdrawable.
Stop trifluoperazine. Continue aripiprazole 15 mg. Repeat AIMS. Prolactin normalises over 2–4 weeks. No QTc concerns with aripiprazole. Review sleep and akathisia at this visit.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Trifluoperazine 10 mg ≈ aripiprazole 15 mg (CPZ equivalence: trifluoperazine 5 mg ≈ CPZ 100 mg ≈ aripiprazole 7.5 mg; therefore trifluoperazine 10 mg ≈ CPZ 200 mg ≈ aripiprazole 15 mg). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

trifluoperazine-to-olanzapine.rationale: Trifluoperazine (high-potency piperazine FGA; high EPS, dystonia risk, tardive dyskinesia risk; moderate anticholinergic activity; high prolactin) to olanzapine (SGA; low EPS; high metabolic risk; high sedation). The FGA→SGA transition should significantly improve EPS burden. Monitor for unmasking of tardive dyskinesia as trifluoperazine is reduced (withdrawal dyskinesias can unmask pre-existing TD). Trifluoperazine has moderate anticholinergic activity — cholinergic rebound is possible but mitigated by olanzapine's M1 blocking activity. Metabolic risk increases on olanzapine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start olanzapine 5 mg nocte. Continue trifluoperazine 10 mg. Baseline metabolic parameters. Document any existing involuntary movements (tardive dyskinesia assessment).
Increase olanzapine to 10 mg (target). Plateau trifluoperazine. EPS burden should begin to improve as olanzapine establishes.
Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. Monitor for emergence of involuntary movements — withdrawal dyskinesias can unmask latent tardive dyskinesia.
Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. EPS improvement expected. Anticholinergic agents used for EPS may now be able to be withdrawn gradually.
Stop trifluoperazine. Continue olanzapine 10 mg. Review EPS and involuntary movements. Metabolic monitoring at 4 and 12 weeks.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Trifluoperazine 10 mg ≈ olanzapine 10 mg (CPZ equivalence: trifluoperazine 5 mg ≈ CPZ 100 mg ≈ olanzapine 2.5 mg; therefore trifluoperazine 10 mg ≈ CPZ 200 mg ≈ olanzapine 5 mg — however clinical practice often uses higher olanzapine targets; dose to clinical response). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

trifluoperazine-to-quetiapine.rationale: Trifluoperazine (high-potency piperazine FGA; high EPS, dystonia risk; moderate anticholinergic activity; high prolactin; moderate QTc) to quetiapine (broad SGA: D2, 5-HT2A, H1, M1, α1/α2; low EPS; metabolic risk; antidepressant profile via norquetiapine). EPS and prolactin should improve significantly. Trifluoperazine has moderate anticholinergic activity — quetiapine's M1 blockade partially mitigates cholinergic rebound. Both carry moderate QTc risk. Unmasking of withdrawal dyskinesias (including tardive dyskinesia) is a risk as trifluoperazine reduces — document baseline involuntary movements. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start quetiapine 100 mg nocte. Continue trifluoperazine 10 mg. Baseline metabolic parameters and AIMS assessment. ECG at baseline. Warn patient about initial sedation and postural hypotension from quetiapine.
Increase quetiapine to 200 mg. Plateau trifluoperazine. EPS burden should begin to ease. Review postural hypotension.
Increase quetiapine to 400 mg (target). Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. Monitor for withdrawal dyskinesias — unmasking of latent tardive dyskinesia is possible at this stage.
Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. Quetiapine well established. Anticholinergic agents used for EPS can now be reviewed for gradual withdrawal.
Stop trifluoperazine. Continue quetiapine 400 mg. Repeat AIMS assessment. Metabolic monitoring at 4 and 12 weeks. QTc check if clinically indicated.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Trifluoperazine 10 mg ≈ quetiapine 400 mg (CPZ equivalence: trifluoperazine 5 mg ≈ CPZ 100 mg ≈ quetiapine 200 mg; therefore trifluoperazine 10 mg ≈ CPZ 200 mg ≈ quetiapine 400 mg). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

trifluoperazine-to-risperidone.rationale: Trifluoperazine (high-potency FGA; D2 dominant; moderate anticholinergic) to risperidone (D2/D3 + 5-HT2A SGA; lower EPS than FGAs; moderate prolactin). EPS should improve but risperidone is not EPS-free. Both drugs elevate prolactin. Both have moderate QTc risk. Trifluoperazine withdrawal can unmask tardive dyskinesia — document baseline movements. Risperidone has minimal anticholinergic activity so it does not buffer cholinergic rebound from trifluoperazine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start risperidone 1 mg. Continue trifluoperazine 10 mg. Baseline AIMS assessment (document existing involuntary movements). ECG at baseline.
Increase risperidone to 2 mg. Plateau trifluoperazine.
Increase risperidone to 4 mg (target). Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. Watch for withdrawal dyskinesias.
Reduce trifluoperazine to 5 mg. EPS burden reducing.
Stop trifluoperazine. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Repeat AIMS at 4 weeks. Anticholinergic agents can be reviewed for withdrawal.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Trifluoperazine 10 mg ≈ risperidone 4 mg (via CPZ equivalence: TFP 5 mg ≈ CPZ 100 mg ≈ risperidone 1 mg; TFP 10 mg ≈ CPZ 200 mg ≈ risperidone 2 mg — however clinical doses often titrated higher; use as starting point). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

valproate-to-carbamazepine.rationale: Valproate to carbamazepine: Indicated for rapid cycling, treatment failure on valproate, or teratogenicity concerns (carbamazepine is Category D but lower teratogenic burden than valproate for non-neural-tube defects). This switch has two pharmacokinetic hazards: (1) Carbamazepine autoinduction — CBZ induces CYP3A4 over 4–6 weeks, reducing its own levels; dose must be increased incrementally. (2) CBZ-epoxide accumulation — valproate inhibits epoxide hydrolase; when co-prescribed, CBZ-epoxide (active toxic metabolite) accumulates to higher levels even with normal CBZ parent compound levels. As valproate is withdrawn, this inhibition is reversed and CBZ-epoxide may initially drop, reducing clinical toxicity. During overlap: monitor for double vision, dizziness, nausea (signs of CBZ-epoxide toxicity). A 'less is more' strategy during overlap: do not push CBZ higher while VPA is still on board. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start carbamazepine 200 mg/day. Continue valproate 1500 mg/day. Baseline LFTs, FBC, Na⁺. Screen for HLA-B*1502 in South/South-East Asian patients before starting. Warn about double vision, dizziness (CBZ-epoxide toxicity during overlap with VPA). Do NOT push CBZ dose rapidly while VPA is on board — epoxide toxicity risk.
Increase carbamazepine to 400 mg/day. Hold valproate. Check CBZ level if neurological side effects (double vision, ataxia). VPA–CBZ-epoxide interaction still active.

Hold carbamazepine at 400 mg during peak VPA-epoxide interaction phase. Begin valproate taper: reduce to 1000 mg/day. As VPA reduces, epoxide hydrolase inhibition reverses and CBZ-epoxide levels will fall — may tolerate CBZ dose increase from next step.
Reduce valproate to 1000 mg/day. Increase carbamazepine to 600 mg/day now that VPA levels are lower. Check CBZ level — autoinduction ongoing.
Reduce valproate to 500 mg/day. Increase carbamazepine to 800 mg/day (target). CBZ autoinduction largely complete by week 6.
Reduce valproate to 200 mg/day. Carbamazepine at full target. Recheck CBZ level to confirm therapeutic (4–10 mg/L for mood disorder).

Stop valproate. Continue carbamazepine 800 mg/day. Recheck CBZ level 2–4 weeks after full valproate withdrawal — enzyme inhibition reversal may increase CBZ clearance, reducing levels. Adjust dose if below therapeutic range.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Not dose-equivalent. Carbamazepine target for bipolar disorder: 400–1200 mg/day titrated to serum level 4–10 mg/L. Note: dose requirements during VPA co-prescription phase will differ from monotherapy due to epoxide interaction — re-establish level after VPA fully withdrawn. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

contraindications: HLA-B*1502 positive (South/South-East Asian patients) — carbamazepine contraindicated.
Current pregnancy or planning pregnancy — discuss teratogenic risk of carbamazepine (neural tube defects ~0.5–1%); valproate remains higher risk. Folic acid 5 mg/day essential if proceeding.

valproate-to-lamotrigine.rationale: This switch has a critical pharmacokinetic hazard: valproate is a potent UGT inhibitor, so the patient will be on a lower-than-normal lamotrigine dose (VPA roughly DOUBLES lamotrigine levels). As valproate is tapered and withdrawn, UGT inhibition is relieved and lamotrigine levels will FALL — potentially losing therapeutic effect (mood relapse risk). Lamotrigine dose MUST be increased in step with the valproate taper. The target monotherapy lamotrigine dose will be roughly DOUBLE the co-prescribed dose. Start lamotrigine at the VPA-adjusted low dose and escalate as VPA is withdrawn. Requires careful timing to avoid a period of subtherapeutic lamotrigine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start lamotrigine at 25 mg every OTHER day for 2 weeks (valproate inhibition is in force — use the VPA co-prescription titration schedule). Hold valproate 1000 mg/day unchanged.
Increase lamotrigine to 25 mg OD. Hold valproate. Monitor for rash — SJS risk is higher when LTG is introduced while VPA is on board.
Increase lamotrigine to 50 mg OD. Begin valproate taper in the next step.
Reduce valproate to 500 mg/day. Increase lamotrigine to 100 mg to compensate for rising LTG clearance as VPA inhibition is partially reversed. Check lamotrigine level if available.
Reduce valproate to 200 mg/day. Increase lamotrigine to 150 mg.
Stop valproate. Lamotrigine monotherapy at 200 mg/day. Assess mood stability and lamotrigine tolerability. Further titration to 400 mg maximum if required.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Not a dose-equivalency switch. Lamotrigine ~50 mg while on valproate ≈ lamotrigine 100 mg monotherapy in terms of plasma levels (VPA roughly doubles LTG levels). The dose is systematically increased as valproate is withdrawn. Target maintenance lamotrigine monotherapy: 100–200 mg/day. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

citations: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines 14th Edition — Lamotrigine drug interactions
Posner K et al. Lamotrigine plasma levels during coadministration with valproate. Epilepsia. 1991.
contraindications: Current pregnancy or planning pregnancy — ensure contraceptive discussion before stopping valproate; see valproate teratogenicity warnings.
Patient on any other UGT inhibitor (e.g. atazanavir) — seek pharmacist review before titrating LTG.

valproate-to-lithium.rationale: Valproate to lithium: Indicated when greater mania prevention is required, during pregnancy (relative — both have teratogenicity but valproate is far higher risk), or where valproate has failed. Lithium must be started at low dose and titrated to serum level (narrow therapeutic index: target 0.6–1.0 mmol/L maintenance). Lithium takes at least 5 half-lives (~5 days) to reach steady state but renal excretion is sensitive to sodium balance, dehydration, and concomitant NSAIDs/ACE inhibitors. Valproate should be maintained throughout lithium titration and tapered only once lithium is at therapeutic level. No pharmacokinetic interaction between valproate and lithium. Valproate withdrawal may cause mood relapse or (rarely) seizures — taper over at least 4–6 weeks. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start lithium 400 mg/day. Continue valproate 1500 mg/day. Baseline renal function, TFT, ECG (if >40 years), weight. Counsel patient: lithium requires twice-daily dosing (Priadel), adequate fluid intake, sick-day rules, and avoidance of NSAIDs. Check lithium level at day 5.
Increase lithium to 800 mg/day if level below target and tolerated. Continue valproate unchanged. Check lithium level at day 12.

Increase lithium to 1000 mg/day if level below target 0.6–1.0 mmol/L (12 h post-dose). Begin valproate taper: reduce to 1000 mg/day. Lithium must be therapeutic before valproate is reduced substantially.
Reduce valproate to 1000 mg/day. Confirm lithium level therapeutic. Monitor mood and check for any signs of lithium side effects (tremor, polyuria, polydipsia).
Reduce valproate to 500 mg/day. Lithium monotherapy providing increasing proportion of cover.
Reduce valproate to 200 mg/day. Recheck lithium level — confirm in target range.
Stop valproate. Continue lithium (dose adjusted to levels). Check lithium level at 4 and 12 weeks. Monitor renal function and TFT 6-monthly. Document EURAP counselling reversal (valproate stopped).

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Not dose-equivalent. Lithium target is defined by serum level (0.6–1.0 mmol/L maintenance; check 12 h post-dose), not weight-based dosing. Typical maintenance dose 800–1200 mg/day but varies significantly by renal function and age. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min) — lithium contraindicated. Do not switch to lithium.
Confirmed or planned pregnancy — discuss risk-benefit carefully; if lithium is chosen, Ebstein's anomaly counselling required.

venlafaxine-to-agomelatine.rationale: Venlafaxine (SNRI; t½ ~5h parent + ~11h metabolite; HIGH discontinuation syndrome risk) to agomelatine (MT1/MT2 agonist; t½ ~2h; no serotonin/noradrenaline reuptake inhibition). Venlafaxine carries the highest discontinuation syndrome risk of all antidepressants — brain zaps, dizziness, nausea, flu-like symptoms can be severe even with short half-life gaps. Taper venlafaxine slowly. Agomelatine can be started during the venlafaxine taper without serotonin syndrome risk (no serotonergic reuptake activity). Baseline LFTs before starting agomelatine. Switch reasons: sexual dysfunction, excessive sweating, blood pressure elevation, weight considerations. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Continue venlafaxine XR 150 mg. CHECK BASELINE LFTs. No serotonin overlap hazard. Warn patient: venlafaxine taper will still cause discontinuation symptoms — this is expected and related to venlafaxine, not agomelatine.
Reduce venlafaxine to 75 mg XR. Continue agomelatine 25 mg. Monitor for discontinuation symptoms — dizziness, brain zaps, sweating. These are mild at this step for most patients.

Reduce venlafaxine to 37.5 mg (lowest available dose). Discontinuation symptoms may intensify at this step — some patients need a slower taper. Consider holding at 37.5 mg for 1–2 additional weeks if symptoms severe.

Stop venlafaxine. Continue agomelatine 25 mg nocte. Venlafaxine discontinuation symptoms peak 1–2 days post-stop then resolve over 1–2 weeks. Titrate agomelatine to 50 mg at 2 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Venlafaxine 150 mg → agomelatine 25 mg (start dose). Different mechanisms — not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

contraindications: Hepatic impairment — agomelatine contraindicated.
ALT >3× ULN at baseline — do not start agomelatine.

venlafaxine-to-desvenlafaxine.rationale: Venlafaxine to desvenlafaxine: Desvenlafaxine is the active metabolite of venlafaxine. Reasons for switch: more predictable pharmacokinetics (desvenlafaxine has less CYP2D6-dependent metabolism — plasma levels are more uniform across CYP2D6 phenotypes), or drug interaction simplification. Both have equivalent SNRI mechanism and high discontinuation syndrome risk. Dose conversion: venlafaxine 75 mg ≈ desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Smooth pharmacological switch — start desvenlafaxine at equivalent dose and taper venlafaxine over 1–2 weeks. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Continue venlafaxine XR 75 mg. Pharmacologically almost identical switch. Both at equivalent doses during the overlap period. No serotonin syndrome risk of clinical significance.
Reduce venlafaxine to 37.5 mg XR. Continue desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Monitor for discontinuation symptoms during venlafaxine reduction.
Stop venlafaxine. Continue desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Titrate to 100 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate (limited additional efficacy but some patients benefit).

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Venlafaxine 75 mg ≈ desvenlafaxine 50 mg (commonly used conversion). Individual variation exists. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

venlafaxine-to-duloxetine.rationale: SNRI-to-SNRI swap, often considered when venlafaxine causes dose-dependent hypertension, sexual dysfunction, or insufficient response. Both drugs share serotonergic and noradrenergic activity; cross-taper can be brief but venlafaxine's very high discontinuation-syndrome risk requires a graded reduction. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start duloxetine 30 mg. Hold venlafaxine XR 150 mg.
Halve venlafaxine to 75 mg XR. Hold duloxetine 30 mg. Watch for serotonergic excess (tremor, hyperreflexia) and discontinuation symptoms.
Reduce venlafaxine to 37.5 mg XR. Increase duloxetine to 60 mg target.
Stop venlafaxine. Continue duloxetine 60 mg. If discontinuation symptoms emerge, slow the final step.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: venlafaxine 150 mg XR ≈ duloxetine 60 mg. Equivalency is approximate; titrate to clinical response. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

venlafaxine-to-mirtazapine.rationale: Switch out of the SSRI/SNRI class entirely after non-response or for tolerability (sexual dysfunction, GI upset, hypertension). Different mechanisms reduce direct serotonergic-overlap concern but venlafaxine's very high discontinuation-syndrome risk requires graded reduction. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start mirtazapine 15 mg at night. Hold venlafaxine XR 150 mg. Counsel re sedation initially.
Halve venlafaxine to 75 mg XR. Increase mirtazapine to 30 mg.
Reduce venlafaxine to 37.5 mg XR. Hold mirtazapine 30 mg. Watch closely for venlafaxine discontinuation symptoms.
Stop venlafaxine. Continue mirtazapine 30 mg. Slow this final step if disc symptoms emerge.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Mirtazapine and venlafaxine are not directly equipotent — mapping reflects typical effective doses for major depression. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

venlafaxine-to-sertraline.rationale: SNRI-to-SSRI swap, often when noradrenergic activity isn't tolerated (sympathomimetic effects, hypertension) or has failed to add benefit. Venlafaxine's very high discontinuation-syndrome risk demands a graded reduction. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start sertraline 25 mg. Hold venlafaxine XR 150 mg.
Halve venlafaxine to 75 mg XR. Increase sertraline to 50 mg. Watch for venlafaxine discontinuation symptoms (electric-shock sensations, dizziness).
Reduce venlafaxine to 37.5 mg XR. Increase sertraline to 100 mg target.
Stop venlafaxine. Continue sertraline 100 mg. If discontinuation symptoms emerge, slow the final step.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Approximate clinical equivalency: venlafaxine 150 mg XR ≈ sertraline 100 mg (Maudsley 14th, conservative mapping for typical effective doses). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

venlafaxine-to-vortioxetine.rationale: Venlafaxine (SNRI; t½ ~5h parent/~11h metabolite; HIGH discontinuation syndrome risk) to vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h). Venlafaxine requires careful, graded tapering — do not stop abruptly. Vortioxetine can be started during the venlafaxine taper. Both drugs are serotonergic — additive effects during overlap are low risk at standard doses. Venlafaxine is not a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor at standard doses — no dose adjustment needed for vortioxetine. After venlafaxine is stopped, vortioxetine's long half-life means it provides smooth ongoing coverage. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start vortioxetine 10 mg. Continue venlafaxine XR 150 mg. Low serotonin syndrome risk at these doses. Counsel patient: venlafaxine taper will cause discontinuation symptoms — these are related to venlafaxine, not vortioxetine.
Reduce venlafaxine to 75 mg XR. Hold vortioxetine. Monitor for discontinuation symptoms — dizziness, brain zaps, sweating.
Reduce venlafaxine to 37.5 mg (lowest available). Discontinuation symptoms may be notable — hold at this dose for longer if severe.
Stop venlafaxine. Continue vortioxetine 10 mg. Titrate vortioxetine to 20 mg at 2 weeks if response inadequate. Vortioxetine's long half-life provides a smooth pharmacokinetic landing.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Venlafaxine 150 mg → vortioxetine 10 mg (start dose; titrate to 20 mg). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

vortioxetine-to-escitalopram.rationale: Vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; multimodal serotonergic; low discontinuation syndrome risk due to long half-life) to escitalopram (SSRI). Vortioxetine's very long half-life provides a natural pharmacokinetic self-taper — plasma levels fall gradually over ~2 weeks after stopping. This substantially reduces discontinuation syndrome risk. A direct switch or minimal overlap approach is clinically reasonable. Both agents are serotonergic — brief overlap may cause mild additive serotonergic effects but serotonin syndrome risk is low at standard doses. Start escitalopram at full therapeutic dose from day 1 of the switch. No CYP2D6 interaction: escitalopram is not a CYP2D6 inhibitor (unlike fluoxetine/paroxetine which would require vortioxetine dose adjustment). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Stop vortioxetine. Start escitalopram 10 mg. Vortioxetine's long half-life (66h) means levels fall gradually — no discontinuation syndrome expected. Brief overlap for clinical safety. Escitalopram has no CYP2D6 inhibition — no dose adjustment needed for vortioxetine residual levels during washout.
Vortioxetine now fully cleared. Continue escitalopram 10 mg. Titrate to 20 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Vortioxetine 20 mg → escitalopram 10 mg (standard effective doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

vortioxetine-to-mirtazapine.rationale: Vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; minimal sedation; cognitive benefits) to mirtazapine (NaSSA: α2-antagonist, 5-HT2/3 antagonist, H1 blocker; significant sedation and weight gain). Switch reasons: sleep problems, need for greater appetite stimulation, or after non-response. Vortioxetine self-tapers due to long half-life. Mirtazapine is 5-HT2 antagonist — combined with vortioxetine's serotonergic effects during brief overlap; low serotonin syndrome risk at standard doses but additive sedation possible. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Stop vortioxetine. Start mirtazapine 15 mg nocte. Vortioxetine levels decline gradually (t½ 66h). Counsel patient about increased sedation and appetite from mirtazapine — take at night. Weight gain is expected and can be significant.
Vortioxetine cleared. Continue mirtazapine 15 mg. Titrate to 30 mg at 2 weeks if response inadequate (30 mg is less sedating than 15 mg due to additional noradrenergic activation at higher doses).

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Vortioxetine 20 mg → mirtazapine 15 mg (start dose; target 30–45 mg). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

vortioxetine-to-sertraline.rationale: Vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; low discontinuation syndrome risk) to sertraline (SSRI; t½ ~26h; moderate discontinuation syndrome risk). Vortioxetine's long half-life provides a natural self-taper. Direct switch is clinically reasonable. Sertraline is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor — but since vortioxetine will be stopped, this interaction is not clinically relevant here (sertraline does not require vortioxetine dose adjustment when used as a replacement). Brief overlap acceptable. Both drugs are serotonergic — standard low serotonin syndrome risk at therapeutic doses. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Stop vortioxetine. Start sertraline 50 mg. Vortioxetine residual plasma levels will persist for ~10–14 days but at declining sub-therapeutic concentrations. Sertraline is a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor — this may theoretically slow vortioxetine clearance slightly during washout but is not clinically significant.
Vortioxetine cleared. Continue sertraline 50 mg. Titrate to 100 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Vortioxetine 20 mg → sertraline 50 mg (standard effective doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

vortioxetine-to-venlafaxine.rationale: Vortioxetine (SMS; t½ ~66h; low discontinuation syndrome risk) to venlafaxine (SNRI; t½ ~5h parent/11h metabolite; HIGH discontinuation syndrome risk). Vortioxetine's long half-life provides natural self-taper — switch is primarily driven by starting venlafaxine. Both are serotonergic — additive serotonergic effects during brief overlap are low risk at standard therapeutic doses. Start venlafaxine at full starting dose from day 1. Vortioxetine residual levels decline gradually — not a clinical concern. Once venlafaxine is established, vortioxetine levels have largely cleared. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Stop vortioxetine. Start venlafaxine XR 75 mg. Vortioxetine's long half-life means residual levels persist 1–2 weeks. Counsel patient about venlafaxine early side effects (nausea, sweating, headache) — take with food. Always use XR formulation.

Vortioxetine largely cleared. Continue venlafaxine XR 75 mg. Titrate to 150 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate. Important: venlafaxine carries high discontinuation syndrome risk — never stop abruptly once established.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Vortioxetine 20 mg → venlafaxine 75 mg (standard starting effective doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

zuclopenthixol-lai-to-zuclopenthixol.rationale: Switching from zuclopenthixol decanoate (Clopixol Depot) to oral zuclopenthixol (Clopixol tablets). Zuclopenthixol decanoate has a t½ of ~17–21 days and continues releasing for ~4–6 weeks after the last injection. Start oral zuclopenthixol when the next depot injection would have been due. Approximate equivalence: zuclopenthixol decanoate 200 mg/2 weeks ≈ oral zuclopenthixol 40 mg/day (Maudsley rough estimate). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Skip next scheduled depot injection. Start oral zuclopenthixol 10 mg/day. Depot continues releasing. Monitor for combined sedation and EPS — zuclopenthixol is notably sedating.
Depot level falling. Increase oral zuclopenthixol to 25 mg/day. Assess sedation, EPS, and clinical response.
Depot substantially cleared (~4 weeks). Oral zuclopenthixol 40 mg/day as primary agent.
Depot cleared. Oral zuclopenthixol monotherapy. Typical range 20–60 mg/day (max 150 mg); titrate to lowest effective dose.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Zuclopenthixol decanoate 200 mg/2 weeks ≈ oral zuclopenthixol 40 mg/day (approximate; Maudsley 15th). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

safetyFlags.title: EPS risk (FGA)
safetyFlags.body: Zuclopenthixol is an FGA with significant EPS risk. Anticholinergic prophylaxis likely needed.

safetyFlags.title: Sedation
safetyFlags.body: Zuclopenthixol is notably sedating among FGAs due to antihistaminic effects. Counsel patients — may affect driving and daily function.

safetyFlags.title: Decanoate tail
safetyFlags.body: Zuclopenthixol decanoate t½ ~17–21 days. Combined oral + depot effect may cause over-sedation in the first 4 weeks.

maudsley15.rationale: Switching strategy matrix derived from The Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines in Psychiatry, 15th Edition. Covers antidepressants (Table 3.7) and mood stabilizers (bipolar chapters). Maudsley uses broad strategy categories rather than rigid day-by-day schedules. When a specific reviewed rule exists for a pair, that takes precedence; otherwise the engine falls back to this class-level lookup. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW — Rashid Razak.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible
rules.detail: Most SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram, citalopram, paroxetine) can be switched directly to another SSRI without a cross-taper or washout. Stop the first drug and start the new one the next day at a low-to-typical starting dose, titrate as tolerated. Watch for discontinuation symptoms with the drug being stopped (especially paroxetine).

rules.headline: Direct switch possible
rules.detail: Stop the current SSRI and start fluoxetine the next day. Fluoxetine's long half-life provides a self-tapering effect that reduces discontinuation symptoms from the original drug. Particularly useful as a 'fluoxetine bridge' from paroxetine.

rules.headline: Stop fluoxetine, wait 4–7 days, start the new SSRI at low dose
rules.detail: Because of fluoxetine's long half-life and the active metabolite norfluoxetine (~7–9 day half-life), a brief washout is needed before starting another SSRI to avoid pharmacokinetic interaction (CYP2D6 inhibition). Start the new SSRI at a low dose and titrate cautiously.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Both drugs are serotonergic — there is mild serotonin syndrome risk during overlap. Reduce the SSRI gradually over 1–2 weeks while introducing and titrating the SNRI. Watch for tremor, hyperreflexia, autonomic instability.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Reduce the SNRI gradually over 1–2 weeks while introducing the SSRI. SNRI discontinuation symptoms (especially venlafaxine — affecting up to 80–100% of patients) are usually the dominant issue — taper slowly and consider hyperbolic tapering for the final reductions.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — fluoxetine bridge useful for venlafaxine
rules.detail: Reduce the SNRI while introducing fluoxetine. The long half-life of fluoxetine offers a 'bridge' effect that mitigates SNRI discontinuation symptoms — especially valuable for venlafaxine, where withdrawal is particularly troublesome.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Both drugs are serotonergic and noradrenergic — mild serotonin syndrome risk during overlap. Reduce the original SNRI gradually while introducing the new one. Beware additive sympathomimetic and gastrointestinal effects.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Mirtazapine has a different mechanism (NaSSA) so theoretically less serotonin syndrome risk, but mirtazapine + SSRI is sometimes used as deliberate augmentation. Reduce the SSRI gradually while introducing mirtazapine 15 mg nocte, increasing as tolerated.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Mirtazapine has a low-to-moderate withdrawal profile but anxiety, irritability and insomnia can occur on stopping. Reduce mirtazapine gradually while introducing the SSRI at a low starting dose.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Reduce the SNRI gradually while introducing mirtazapine. Useful combination: the SNRI 'covers' SNRI withdrawal while mirtazapine is being titrated up. Watch for excessive sedation as mirtazapine is added.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Reduce mirtazapine gradually while introducing the SNRI. Discontinuation symptoms with mirtazapine are uncommon but possible — anxiety and insomnia are typical.

rules.headline: Stop the SSRI, wait 14 days, then start moclobemide
rules.detail: Moclobemide is a reversible MAOI (RIMA). Despite the reversibility, a 14-day washout from a serotonergic agent is required before starting moclobemide to avoid serotonin syndrome. Fluoxetine requires a 5-week (35-day) washout because of norfluoxetine.

rules.headline: Stop fluoxetine, wait 5–6 weeks, then start moclobemide
rules.detail: Fluoxetine's 5-week (35-day) washout before any MAOI — including the reversible moclobemide — is non-negotiable. Norfluoxetine's 7–9 day half-life means trace levels persist for over a month.

rules.headline: Taper the SNRI, wait 14 days, then start moclobemide
rules.detail: Cross-tapering serotonergic drugs with an MAOI risks serotonin syndrome. Taper the SNRI to zero (consider hyperbolic taper for venlafaxine) and wait 14 days before starting moclobemide.

rules.headline: Taper mirtazapine, wait 14 days, then start moclobemide
rules.detail: Although mirtazapine is not a primary serotonergic agent, a 14-day washout is recommended before starting any MAOI for safety.

rules.headline: Stop moclobemide, wait 24 hours, then start the SSRI
rules.detail: Moclobemide is a reversible MAOI — its enzyme inhibition resolves within 24 hours of stopping. After this short washout, an SSRI can be started.

rules.headline: Stop moclobemide, wait 24 hours, then start fluoxetine
rules.detail: After 24 hours of moclobemide clearance, fluoxetine can be safely started.

rules.headline: Stop moclobemide, wait 24 hours, then start the SNRI
rules.detail: After 24 hours of moclobemide clearance, an SNRI can be safely started. Titrate cautiously.

rules.headline: Stop moclobemide, wait 24 hours, then start mirtazapine
rules.detail: After 24 hours of moclobemide clearance, mirtazapine can be safely started.

rules.headline: Stop the MAOI, wait 14 days, then start the SSRI
rules.detail: Irreversible MAOIs (phenelzine, tranylcypromine) require a full 14-day washout before any serotonergic drug to allow new MAO enzyme synthesis. Starting an SSRI before 14 days risks fatal serotonin syndrome.

rules.headline: Stop the MAOI, wait 14 days, then start fluoxetine
rules.detail: Same as for any SSRI: 14-day washout from the irreversible MAOI is required.

rules.headline: Stop the MAOI, wait 14 days, then start the SNRI
rules.detail: 14-day washout from the irreversible MAOI is required before any serotonergic agent.

rules.headline: Stop the MAOI, wait 14 days, then start mirtazapine
rules.detail: Although mirtazapine is not a primary serotonergic agent, a 14-day washout from any irreversible MAOI is recommended.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Both drugs are serotonergic. Reduce the SSRI gradually over 1–2 weeks while introducing vortioxetine at 5–10 mg. Vortioxetine's long half-life (~66 h) means it accumulates slowly — titrate up once the SSRI is fully stopped. Watch for additive serotonergic effects during overlap.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — vortioxetine self-tapers due to long half-life
rules.detail: Vortioxetine's long half-life (~66 h) provides a degree of self-tapering on stopping, making discontinuation syndrome uncommon. Reduce vortioxetine gradually while introducing the SSRI at a standard starting dose. Serotonin syndrome risk during overlap is low but not zero.

rules.headline: Stop fluoxetine, wait 5–7 days, then start vortioxetine at half dose
rules.detail: Fluoxetine is a potent CYP2D6 inhibitor that roughly doubles vortioxetine plasma levels. Even after stopping fluoxetine, inhibition persists for 5–7 days due to norfluoxetine's long half-life. Start vortioxetine at 5 mg (half the usual 10 mg starting dose) and titrate cautiously once CYP2D6 inhibition has resolved.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible — vortioxetine's long half-life bridges the transition
rules.detail: Stop vortioxetine and start fluoxetine the next day at a standard starting dose. Vortioxetine's long half-life (~66 h) provides gradual decline. Note: once fluoxetine is established, its CYP2D6 inhibition would raise vortioxetine levels if the switch is reversed — but in the forward direction this is not a concern.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Both are serotonergic. Reduce the SNRI gradually (especially venlafaxine — prone to troublesome discontinuation symptoms) while introducing vortioxetine at 5–10 mg. Vortioxetine's long half-life means it accumulates over several days — titrate once the SNRI is stopped or near-stopped.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Reduce vortioxetine while introducing the SNRI. The overlap period carries mild serotonin syndrome risk. Vortioxetine's long half-life means even after stopping the dose, serotonergic activity declines slowly — avoid aggressive titration of the SNRI during this phase.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Mirtazapine is not primarily serotonergic, but serotonin syndrome risk exists during overlap with any serotonergic drug. Reduce mirtazapine gradually while introducing vortioxetine at 5–10 mg nocte. Watch for insomnia as mirtazapine's sedating antihistaminergic effect is withdrawn.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Reduce vortioxetine while introducing mirtazapine 15 mg nocte. Vortioxetine's long half-life provides gradual serotonergic decline — this makes the overlap period relatively low risk for serotonin syndrome.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible — agomelatine is not serotonergic
rules.detail: Agomelatine acts via melatonin receptors (MT1/MT2) and 5-HT2C antagonism, not via serotonin transporter inhibition. There is no meaningful serotonin syndrome risk when switching FROM vortioxetine TO agomelatine. Stop vortioxetine and start agomelatine the same or next day. Ensure LFTs are checked at baseline before starting agomelatine.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible
rules.detail: Agomelatine has no clinically significant drug interactions with vortioxetine. Stop agomelatine and start vortioxetine the same or next day at 10 mg. No washout required. Note: agomelatine requires LFT monitoring — confirm no hepatic dysfunction before starting any new drug.

rules.headline: Stop vortioxetine, wait 14 days, then start moclobemide
rules.detail: Vortioxetine is serotonergic — despite moclobemide's reversibility, a 14-day washout from any serotonergic agent is required before starting moclobemide to avoid serotonin syndrome. Vortioxetine's long half-life (~66 h) means levels are negligible after 14 days.

rules.headline: Stop moclobemide, wait 24 hours, then start vortioxetine
rules.detail: Moclobemide is a reversible MAOI; MAO-A inhibition resolves within 24 hours of stopping. After this washout, vortioxetine can be safely started at 10 mg.

rules.headline: Stop vortioxetine, wait 14 days, then start the MAOI
rules.detail: A 14-day washout from vortioxetine (a serotonergic drug) is required before starting any irreversible MAOI to prevent serotonin syndrome. Vortioxetine's 66-hour half-life means levels are negligible by day 14.

rules.headline: Stop the MAOI, wait 14 days, then start vortioxetine
rules.detail: Irreversible MAOIs require a full 14-day washout before any serotonergic agent. After 14 days, vortioxetine can be started at 5–10 mg and titrated as tolerated.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible — agomelatine is not serotonergic
rules.detail: Agomelatine's melatonergic mechanism means there is no meaningful serotonergic overlap when switching from an SSRI. Stop the SSRI and start agomelatine 25 mg nocte on the next day. Obtain baseline LFTs before starting agomelatine. Be aware that agomelatine may take 2–4 weeks to reach full effect — brief discontinuation symptoms from the SSRI (especially paroxetine) may occur.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible
rules.detail: Stop agomelatine and start the SSRI the same or next day at a standard starting dose. Agomelatine has no serotonergic activity — there is no serotonin syndrome risk during this transition.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible — but allow 5–7 days for fluoxetine CYP effect to resolve
rules.detail: Agomelatine is primarily a CYP1A2 substrate (not CYP2D6), so fluoxetine's CYP2D6 inhibition does not meaningfully affect it. A serotonin syndrome washout is not required as agomelatine is not serotonergic. However, a brief 5–7 day gap after stopping fluoxetine is pragmatic to allow any residual CYP inhibition to resolve before agomelatine titration. Obtain baseline LFTs before starting agomelatine.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible
rules.detail: Stop agomelatine and start fluoxetine the next day at 20 mg. No washout required. Fluoxetine is a CYP2D6 inhibitor but agomelatine is a CYP1A2 substrate — no pharmacokinetic interaction in this direction.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible — but taper SNRI first to manage discontinuation
rules.detail: Agomelatine is not serotonergic so there is no serotonin syndrome risk when adding it to a tapering SNRI. Taper the SNRI gradually (especially venlafaxine — hyperbolic taper for high doses) and start agomelatine 25 mg nocte once the SNRI is stopped or at a low dose. Obtain baseline LFTs.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible
rules.detail: Stop agomelatine and start the SNRI at a standard starting dose the same or next day. No serotonin syndrome risk — agomelatine is not serotonergic.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible — monitor for insomnia on stopping mirtazapine
rules.detail: Mirtazapine's sedating antihistaminergic effect will be lost when stopped. Start agomelatine 25 mg nocte while tapering mirtazapine. Agomelatine itself has a mild sleep-onset benefit via melatonin agonism, but the transition period may involve rebound insomnia. Obtain baseline LFTs.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible
rules.detail: Stop agomelatine and start mirtazapine 15 mg nocte the same or next day. Mirtazapine's sedative effect may be prominent initially — warn the patient.

rules.headline: Stop agomelatine, wait 24–48 hours, then start moclobemide
rules.detail: Agomelatine is not a classical serotonergic drug, but caution is warranted given its 5-HT2C antagonism. A brief 1–2 day gap after stopping agomelatine before starting any MAOI is prudent.

rules.headline: Stop moclobemide, wait 24 hours, then start agomelatine
rules.detail: Moclobemide's reversible MAO-A inhibition resolves within 24 hours. Agomelatine is not a serotonergic drug, so the risk of serotonin syndrome is very low. A 24-hour gap is sufficient for safety.

rules.headline: Stop agomelatine, wait 14 days, then start the MAOI
rules.detail: While agomelatine is not primarily serotonergic, a standard 14-day conservative washout before starting an irreversible MAOI is appropriate given agomelatine's 5-HT2C activity.

rules.headline: Stop the MAOI, wait 14 days, then start agomelatine
rules.detail: Standard 14-day irreversible MAOI washout applies before introducing any psychotropic agent. After 14 days, agomelatine 25 mg nocte can be started. Obtain baseline LFTs.

rules.headline: Stop fluvoxamine, wait 7 days for CYP1A2 recovery, then start agomelatine at 12.5 mg
rules.detail: Fluvoxamine is a potent CYP1A2 inhibitor and agomelatine is a CYP1A2 substrate — co-administration is absolutely contraindicated. After stopping fluvoxamine, CYP1A2 activity recovers over approximately 1 week. Wait at least 7 days before starting agomelatine, then begin at a cautiously low dose (12.5 mg if available, or 25 mg with extra LFT vigilance) as residual CYP1A2 inhibition may persist.

rules.headline: Stop agomelatine, then start fluvoxamine — do NOT re-start agomelatine while on fluvoxamine
rules.detail: Stop agomelatine and start fluvoxamine at its standard starting dose. This direction does not carry a specific pharmacokinetic interaction risk — the concern is the reverse (fluvoxamine ON agomelatine). Counsel the patient explicitly that agomelatine must never be restarted while taking fluvoxamine.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — load valproate while tapering lithium
rules.detail: Lithium and valproate can be overlapped safely. Start valproate at 200–400 mg/day and titrate to a therapeutic level while reducing lithium over 4–6 weeks. Both are antimanic agents with complementary mechanisms. Monitor lithium levels through the taper — lithium has a narrow therapeutic window (target 0.6–0.8 mmol/L for maintenance). Check renal function before and 3 months after lithium is stopped. If mood stability is fragile, slow the lithium taper or consider a longer overlap period.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — titrate lithium to level before tapering valproate
rules.detail: Start lithium and titrate to a therapeutic serum level (0.6–0.8 mmol/L) before beginning the valproate taper — do not taper valproate until lithium is stable. Valproate withdrawal can precipitate mania; cover is essential throughout. Reduce valproate over 4–6 weeks once lithium is established. Ensure renal function and thyroid function are checked before starting lithium.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — titrate lamotrigine slowly before tapering lithium
rules.detail: Lamotrigine requires slow titration (standard schedule: 25 mg/day for 2 weeks, then 50 mg/day for 2 weeks, then increase by 50 mg every 2 weeks) to minimise Stevens-Johnson syndrome risk. Do not begin tapering lithium until lamotrigine reaches 100–150 mg/day and the patient is clinically stable. Total transition time is typically 10–12 weeks. Lithium and lamotrigine can be safely co-prescribed during the overlap. Lamotrigine has better evidence for bipolar depression than mania — ensure the indication aligns.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — establish lithium level before tapering lamotrigine
rules.detail: Start lithium and titrate to a therapeutic serum level (0.6–0.8 mmol/L) before beginning lamotrigine taper. Lamotrigine levels are not affected by lithium (no pharmacokinetic interaction). Taper lamotrigine over 4–6 weeks once lithium is stable. Lamotrigine can generally be tapered more rapidly than it was introduced, but abrupt discontinuation should be avoided due to risk of rebound seizures and mood instability.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — allow 4 weeks for carbamazepine autoinduction before tapering lithium
rules.detail: Carbamazepine undergoes hepatic autoinduction of its own metabolism over 3–4 weeks after initiation — initial doses that produce therapeutic levels become sub-therapeutic as induction occurs. Start carbamazepine at 100–200 mg/day, check levels at 2 weeks, increase to reach target (4–10 mg/L), and allow 4 weeks before beginning lithium taper. Monitor CBZ levels closely during titration. CBZ mildly increases renal lithium clearance — lithium levels may fall slightly as CBZ is added; check lithium level during the overlap.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — monitor lithium level as carbamazepine tapers
rules.detail: Start lithium and titrate to therapeutic level (0.6–0.8 mmol/L) while carbamazepine is still at full dose. As CBZ tapers, the mild induction of renal lithium clearance reduces — lithium levels may rise. Recheck lithium level at each CBZ dose reduction step. Taper carbamazepine over 4–6 weeks. Carbamazepine withdrawal can rarely trigger seizures; if the patient has a seizure history, taper more slowly.

rules.headline: Complex switch — pharmacokinetic interaction in both directions; specialist guidance recommended
rules.detail: This switch carries two simultaneous pharmacokinetic hazards: (1) Valproate inhibits carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide hydrolase — as carbamazepine is added, the toxic epoxide metabolite accumulates, causing CBZ toxicity (diplopia, ataxia, nausea) at seemingly normal CBZ plasma levels. Monitor for toxicity symptoms, not just CBZ levels. (2) Carbamazepine induces valproate metabolism — as CBZ titrates up, VPA levels fall; the VPA dose may need increasing, or the VPA taper may need slowing. Start carbamazepine at a low dose (100 mg/day) and titrate very slowly while monitoring for epoxide toxicity. Overlap should be minimised — transition to CBZ while tapering VPA, ideally with specialist oversight.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — valproate dose requirements increase while CBZ is present, then fall after CBZ stops
rules.detail: Carbamazepine is a potent enzyme inducer that significantly increases valproate metabolism. While CBZ is present, higher-than-usual valproate doses will be needed to achieve therapeutic levels. As CBZ is tapered and enzyme induction resolves, valproate levels will rise — plan to reduce the valproate dose when CBZ is stopped or near-stopped, otherwise toxicity (tremor, nausea, encephalopathy) may occur. Start valproate at a cautious dose, titrate to levels, and closely re-check VPA levels 1–2 weeks after each CBZ reduction.

rules.headline: Caution — valproate doubles lamotrigine levels; taper LTG carefully as VPA is added
rules.detail: Valproate inhibits lamotrigine glucuronidation (UGT1A4), approximately doubling lamotrigine plasma levels. As valproate is introduced and titrated up, lamotrigine levels will rise — this risks LTG toxicity (dizziness, diplopia, ataxia) even if the LTG dose is unchanged. As VPA is added, halve the lamotrigine dose to compensate for the inhibitory effect. Once VPA is at a stable dose and LTG has been reduced, taper LTG to zero. Conversely, if LTG is being completely stopped, the VPA-induced LTG elevation is less relevant, but monitor for LTG toxicity during the early overlap.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — carbamazepine halves lamotrigine levels via enzyme induction
rules.detail: Carbamazepine is a potent inducer of UGT1A4 and CYP enzymes that approximately halves lamotrigine plasma levels. As CBZ is added, LTG levels will fall — if the LTG dose is not compensated, under-treatment may occur during the transition. Since the goal is to switch TO carbamazepine (and stop LTG), the falling LTG levels during the CBZ titration phase are less problematic, but ensure CBZ reaches therapeutic levels (4–10 mg/L) before lamotrigine is fully stopped to prevent a coverage gap. Allow 4 weeks for CBZ autoinduction to stabilise before stopping LTG.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously over 2–4 weeks
rules.detail: Most SGA-to-SGA switches can be managed with a 2–4 week cross-taper. Overlap both drugs during titration. Key considerations vary by pair: switching TO olanzapine or quetiapine carries high metabolic risk — monitor weight and glucose. Switching AWAY from olanzapine/quetiapine may cause rebound insomnia and anxiety (H1/α1 withdrawal) as the dose falls below 200 mg (quetiapine) or 7.5 mg (olanzapine). Prolactin will rise when switching TO risperidone or amisulpride; normalisation expected when switching AWAY. Amisulpride and sulpiride are renally cleared — no CYP interactions to consider. Check the individual drug profiles for QTc risk if cardiac concerns apply.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — EPS risk increases when introducing an FGA
rules.detail: Switching from an SGA to an FGA increases the risk of extrapyramidal side effects (EPS: akathisia, parkinsonism, dystonia). Cross-taper over 2–4 weeks. If the patient has had EPS previously, consider starting or continuing anticholinergic cover (e.g. benzhexol). QTc monitoring is important if switching TO haloperidol or chlorpromazine — both carry high QTc risk. Metabolic burden typically improves when leaving high-metabolic SGAs (olanzapine, quetiapine). Trifluoperazine and haloperidol are high-EPS agents — titrate cautiously.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — significant akathisia risk when introducing aripiprazole
rules.detail: Aripiprazole's D2 partial agonism causes akathisia when introduced while D2 receptors are still occupied by a full antagonist SGA. The higher the prior SGA dose, the more pronounced the akathisia risk. Plateau cross-taper is preferred: start aripiprazole while keeping the SGA at full dose, then taper the SGA only after aripiprazole is tolerated at a therapeutic dose (15–30 mg).
