Warn the patient explicitly about akathisia before switching. Have a low threshold to add propranolol 10–30 mg twice daily if akathisia occurs. Metabolic improvement is expected when moving away from olanzapine or quetiapine.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — EPS improves, metabolic and sedation profile changes
rules.detail: Switching from an FGA to an SGA typically improves EPS but alters the metabolic and sedation profile. Cross-taper over 2–4 weeks. If switching TO olanzapine or quetiapine, counsel about weight gain, sedation, and glucose dysregulation — obtain baseline metabolics. Patients on long-term FGAs may have tardive dyskinesia that becomes unmasked as dopamine blockade is reduced — monitor during taper. If the patient is on an anticholinergic agent for FGA-related EPS, review whether it can be tapered once the FGA is stopped. Prolactin will normalise if switching to aripiprazole.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — monitor EPS and QTc throughout
rules.detail: FGA-to-FGA switches carry additive EPS risk during the overlap period. Cross-taper over 2–4 weeks. Monitor closely for worsening EPS and maintain anticholinergic cover if needed. QTc additive risk is a specific concern if both drugs carry high QTc burden (e.g. haloperidol and chlorpromazine) — obtain ECG before and during the switch. Sulpiride and amisulpride are renally cleared benzamides — lower EPS burden than phenothiazines or butyrophenones. High-potency FGAs (haloperidol, trifluoperazine) carry higher EPS risk than low-potency agents (chlorpromazine, sulpiride).

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — akathisia risk when introducing aripiprazole from a full-antagonist FGA
rules.detail: The transition from a full D2 antagonist FGA to aripiprazole (partial agonist) carries substantial akathisia risk. The higher the pre-existing D2 occupancy, the more pronounced the effect. Use a plateau cross-taper: start aripiprazole at 10–15 mg while maintaining the FGA at its current dose, wait 1–2 weeks, then taper the FGA. Warn the patient about akathisia early and check at every visit. Propranolol 10–30 mg twice daily can manage akathisia if it occurs. Metabolic profile will improve.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously
rules.detail: Switching from aripiprazole (partial agonist) to an SGA is generally straightforward. Cross-taper over 2–4 weeks. The SGA's full D2 antagonism will establish progressively as aripiprazole is tapered — there is no akathisia risk with this direction. Key considerations: if switching TO olanzapine or quetiapine, counsel about metabolic changes and obtain baseline weight and glucose. If switching TO risperidone or amisulpride, prolactin will rise — counsel patients with prior prolactin sensitivity.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — EPS risk increases when introducing FGA
rules.detail: Switching from aripiprazole to an FGA will increase EPS risk and prolactin. Cross-taper over 2–4 weeks. Consider starting or continuing anticholinergic cover when introducing the FGA, especially high-potency agents (haloperidol, trifluoperazine). There is no akathisia risk in this direction — the opposite of switching TO aripiprazole. QTc monitoring required for haloperidol and chlorpromazine.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — follow the LAI's initiation protocol
rules.detail: When switching from an oral SGA to an SGA LAI, follow the specific LAI's initiation protocol. Paliperidone palmitate (Invega Sustenna) uses a two-dose deltoid loading protocol (150 mg day 1, 100 mg day 8) — no oral overlap required. Risperidone Consta requires 21 days of oral risperidone cover after the first injection. During the loading phase, the oral SGA can be continued for antipsychotic cover then tapered once the LAI reaches therapeutic levels. Counsel the patient on injection schedule, site rotation, and cold-chain handling.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap for Abilify Maintena
rules.detail: Aripiprazole LAI (Abilify Maintena) requires a mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap after the first 400 mg injection, as the microsphere depot takes this time to establish therapeutic levels. Akathisia risk is significant when introducing aripiprazole into a patient on a full-antagonist SGA — use a plateau cross-taper: administer Maintena and start the oral aripiprazole overlap while keeping the current SGA at full dose. Taper the SGA only after the 14-day oral overlap is complete and the depot is therapeutic.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — continue oral SGA during FGA LAI loading phase
rules.detail: FGA LAIs (zuclopenthixol decanoate, flupenthixol decanoate, fluphenazine decanoate) have a slow absorption phase after each injection — therapeutic levels take 2–4 weeks to establish. Continue the oral SGA during the LAI loading phase. EPS risk increases when introducing an FGA LAI — maintain or start anticholinergic cover. Once the LAI has reached steady state (typically by the second injection), taper and stop the oral SGA. Monitor for tardive dyskinesia with long-term FGA LAI use.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — follow the SGA LAI's initiation protocol
rules.detail: When switching from an oral FGA to an SGA LAI, follow the specific depot's initiation protocol. Paliperidone palmitate uses a two-dose deltoid loading protocol (150 mg day 1, 100 mg day 8) and does not require oral paliperidone overlap. Continue the oral FGA during the loading period for antipsychotic cover, then taper. EPS should improve as the FGA is stopped. Review and taper anticholinergic cover once the FGA is fully stopped. Prolactin may remain elevated with paliperidone palmitate — counsel accordingly.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap; akathisia risk
rules.detail: Aripiprazole LAI requires a mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap. When the from-drug is an FGA, the high pre-existing D2 occupancy makes akathisia particularly likely. Use a plateau cross-taper: start Maintena 400 mg and the 14-day oral aripiprazole while keeping the FGA at full dose. Taper the FGA only after the oral overlap is complete. Propranolol 10–30 mg twice daily for akathisia management if needed.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — continue oral FGA during LAI loading (typically 4 weeks)
rules.detail: FGA LAI initiation requires 4 weeks of oral FGA overlap while the depot establishes therapeutic levels. The standard loading dose for haloperidol decanoate is 10–15× the daily oral dose (capped at 100 mg first injection). For zuclopenthixol, flupenthixol and fluphenazine decanoate, the first injection establishes slowly — continue oral cover at a reduced dose (typically 50%) for 4 weeks. QTc monitoring is essential if the FGA or its LAI carries high QTc risk (particularly haloperidol decanoate). Monitor for cumulative EPS.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — follow the SGA LAI's initiation protocol
rules.detail: Switching from aripiprazole to an SGA LAI is relatively straightforward. For paliperidone palmitate, use the two-dose deltoid loading protocol (150 mg day 1, 100 mg day 8) while continuing oral aripiprazole. Taper aripiprazole once the LAI loading is complete (after day 8). No akathisia risk in this direction — the SGA is a full antagonist. Prolactin will rise with paliperidone palmitate — counsel the patient.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — continue oral aripiprazole during FGA LAI loading (4 weeks)
rules.detail: Continue oral aripiprazole during the 4-week FGA LAI loading phase. EPS risk increases when introducing an FGA LAI — start or maintain anticholinergic cover. No akathisia risk in this direction. Monitor QTc if the FGA LAI carries high QTc burden. Taper and stop oral aripiprazole once the LAI has reached steady state (second injection onwards).

rules.headline: Overlap oral SGA during LAI tail — allow for depot washout
rules.detail: When discontinuing an SGA LAI and starting an oral SGA, begin the oral SGA at the time the next injection would have been due (or one injection cycle before if bridging is needed). The depot has a long elimination tail — for paliperidone palmitate the effective half-life is ~25–50 days, meaning therapeutic levels persist for weeks after the last injection. The oral SGA overlaps the LAI tail, then continues as monotherapy. No specific loading required. Counsel the patient on the transition from injectable to oral dosing.

rules.headline: Start oral FGA at next injection interval — EPS risk increases
rules.detail: Begin the oral FGA at the time the LAI injection would next be due. The SGA LAI's long elimination tail provides cover during the transition. EPS risk increases when introducing an FGA — start anticholinergic cover. QTc monitoring for high-risk FGAs. The long depot tail means both drugs are present for several weeks — monitor for additive side effects.

rules.headline: Start aripiprazole at next injection interval — akathisia risk from LAI tail overlap
rules.detail: Start oral aripiprazole 10–15 mg at the time the next LAI injection would be due. The SGA LAI's long tail means full D2 occupancy persists — this is the window of highest akathisia risk. Consider starting aripiprazole at a lower dose (5–10 mg) and titrating cautiously. Monitor for akathisia at 1–2 weeks. The LAI tail provides antipsychotic cover, so there is no gap risk — the priority is managing the partial-agonist transition period.

rules.headline: Start oral SGA at next injection interval — FGA LAI tail provides cover
rules.detail: Begin the oral SGA at the time the next FGA LAI injection would have been due (i.e. skip the injection and start the oral drug instead). The FGA depot has a long tail (haloperidol decanoate: effective half-life ~21 days; fluphenazine/flupenthixol/zuclopenthixol: similar). The oral SGA can be titrated up while the FGA LAI level declines. EPS should improve as the FGA level falls. Tardive dyskinesia unmasking is possible with long-term FGA LAI patients — monitor carefully. Metabolic baseline before starting any new SGA.

rules.headline: Start new oral FGA at next injection interval — avoid double FGA loading
rules.detail: When transitioning from an FGA LAI to a different oral FGA, start the new oral FGA at the time the last injection's effects are declining (typically around the next injection interval). Avoid double-loading — the LAI tail will provide some cover. Monitor for cumulative EPS from both FGA agents. QTc additive risk if both carry high QTc burden (e.g. haloperidol and chlorpromazine) — ECG monitoring.

rules.headline: Start aripiprazole at next injection interval — akathisia risk from FGA LAI tail
rules.detail: Start oral aripiprazole 10–15 mg at the time the next FGA LAI injection would be due (skipping the injection). The FGA depot tail means D2 occupancy persists for weeks — the window of highest akathisia risk. Start aripiprazole at a low dose (10 mg) and titrate cautiously. If akathisia occurs, propranolol 10–30 mg twice daily. The FGA LAI tail provides antipsychotic cover during transition.

rules.headline: Start SGA LAI at next injection interval — FGA tail covers gap
rules.detail: When switching between FGA LAI and SGA LAI (e.g. fluphenazine decanoate to paliperidone palmitate), administer the first SGA LAI injection at the time the next FGA injection would have been due. For paliperidone palmitate, use the full two-dose deltoid loading protocol (150 mg day 1, 100 mg day 8) — the FGA tail provides cover during loading. EPS should improve progressively as the FGA level declines. Prolactin remains elevated with paliperidone. No oral overlap required for PP-LAI loading.

rules.headline: Start aripiprazole LAI at next injection interval — mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap; akathisia risk
rules.detail: Administer Abilify Maintena 400 mg at the time the next FGA LAI injection would have been due. The 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap is mandatory. The FGA LAI tail provides antipsychotic cover during the initiation period. Akathisia risk is significant — the residual FGA occupancy overlaps with aripiprazole's partial agonism. Start the oral aripiprazole at 10 mg and monitor closely. Propranolol 10–30 mg twice daily if akathisia occurs. Taper and stop oral aripiprazole at day 14.

rules.headline: Switch FGA LAI at the next injection interval
rules.detail: When switching between two FGA LAIs, administer the first dose of the new depot at the time the next injection of the old depot would have been due. No oral cover is required as the old LAI's tail provides a smooth bridge. Dose equivalence between FGA depots varies — consult the Maudsley dose-equivalence tables. Monitor EPS throughout; cumulative EPS risk from two FGA agents overlapping is real. QTc monitoring required if switching between high-QTc agents.

rules.headline: Start oral SGA when aripiprazole LAI level begins to decline
rules.detail: Aripiprazole LAI has a long effective half-life (~46 days from Maintena). When stopping and switching to an oral SGA, start the oral drug at the time the next injection would have been due. No akathisia risk in this direction. Titrate the oral SGA to therapeutic dose while the LAI level declines. Metabolic monitoring if switching to a high-metabolic SGA (olanzapine, quetiapine). Prolactin will rise if switching to risperidone or amisulpride.

rules.headline: Start oral FGA when aripiprazole LAI level begins to decline — EPS risk increases
rules.detail: Start the oral FGA at the time the next aripiprazole LAI injection would have been due. The aripiprazole LAI long tail provides antipsychotic cover during the transition. EPS increases with the introduction of an FGA — start anticholinergic cover. QTc monitoring for high-risk FGAs. No akathisia risk in this direction.

rules.headline: Start oral aripiprazole at the time of the next injection — same active molecule
rules.detail: Aripiprazole LAI (Abilify Maintena) and oral aripiprazole share the same active molecule. When discontinuing the depot and switching to oral, start oral aripiprazole 10–15 mg on the day the next injection would have been due. The LAI depot has a long elimination half-life (~46 days) so a significant reservoir remains — the oral dose supplements rather than replaces the depot level initially. No washout, loading, or antipsychotic gap to manage. Titrate oral aripiprazole to the therapeutic dose used previously.

rules.headline: Switch at next injection interval — aripiprazole LAI tail provides cover; EPS risk increases
rules.detail: When switching from aripiprazole LAI to an FGA LAI, administer the first FGA LAI dose at the time the next aripiprazole injection would have been due (skipping the aripiprazole injection). The aripiprazole LAI long tail (~46-day effective half-life) provides antipsychotic cover for several weeks. EPS risk increases significantly when introducing an FGA LAI — start anticholinergic cover early. For FGA LAIs requiring oral cover (zuclopenthixol, flupenthixol, fluphenazine decanoate), add oral cover at a reduced dose for 4 weeks alongside the first depot injection. QTc monitoring required for the new FGA LAI. No akathisia risk in this direction — moving away from partial agonism to full D2 antagonism.

rules.headline: Switch at next injection interval — follow the SGA LAI initiation protocol
rules.detail: When switching from aripiprazole LAI to an SGA LAI (e.g. paliperidone palmitate), administer the first SGA LAI dose at the time the next aripiprazole LAI injection would have been due. The aripiprazole LAI long tail provides antipsychotic cover during the SGA LAI loading phase. For paliperidone palmitate, use the two-dose deltoid loading protocol (150 mg day 1, 100 mg day 8). No oral overlap required for PP-LAI loading. No akathisia risk switching in this direction. Prolactin will rise with paliperidone palmitate — counsel the patient.

rules.headline: Switch at next injection interval — SGA LAI tail covers gap; EPS risk increases
rules.detail: When switching from an SGA LAI (e.g. paliperidone palmitate) to an FGA LAI, administer the first FGA LAI dose at the time the next SGA injection would have been due. The SGA LAI long tail (paliperidone palmitate effective half-life ~25–50 days) provides antipsychotic cover during the FGA LAI loading phase. EPS risk increases when introducing an FGA LAI — start anticholinergic cover early, especially for high-potency FGA LAIs (fluphenazine, zuclopenthixol, flupenthixol decanoate). Continue oral FGA cover at a reduced dose for 4 weeks alongside the first FGA depot injection as the LAI establishes. QTc monitoring required. Tardive dyskinesia risk increases with long-term FGA LAI use.

rules.headline: Switch at next injection interval — mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap; akathisia risk from SGA LAI tail
rules.detail: Administer aripiprazole LAI (Abilify Maintena 400 mg) at the time the next SGA LAI injection would have been due. The mandatory 14-day oral aripiprazole overlap must be started concurrently with the first Maintena injection. The SGA LAI tail provides antipsychotic cover. Akathisia is a significant risk: the residual SGA LAI D2 occupancy overlaps with aripiprazole's partial agonism during the initiation period. Warn the patient explicitly; have propranolol 10–30 mg twice daily ready. Taper and stop oral aripiprazole at day 14. Prolactin will normalise as the SGA LAI clears.

rules.headline: Stop fluoxetine, wait 5–7 days for CYP2D6 activity to recover, then start the SNRI at low dose
rules.detail: Fluoxetine is a potent CYP2D6 inhibitor. Most SNRIs are CYP2D6 substrates (venlafaxine's active metabolite ODV is generated by CYP2D6; duloxetine is also partially CYP2D6-mediated). Initiating an SNRI while fluoxetine/norfluoxetine CYP2D6 inhibition is present risks elevated SNRI exposure and additive serotonergic effects. After stopping fluoxetine, wait approximately 5–7 days for the main phase of CYP2D6 inhibition to resolve before starting the SNRI at its lowest available dose. Titrate the SNRI cautiously over the first 2–3 weeks; CYP2D6 activity continues to recover for several weeks until norfluoxetine is fully eliminated (~5–6 weeks).

rules.headline: Stop fluoxetine, wait 5–7 days, then start mirtazapine at low dose
rules.detail: Mirtazapine is a CYP2D6 and CYP1A2 substrate. Fluoxetine's potent CYP2D6 inhibition raises mirtazapine plasma levels when both are present. Stopping fluoxetine and immediately starting mirtazapine risks supra-therapeutic mirtazapine exposure (excessive sedation, weight gain) until the CYP2D6 inhibition resolves. Allow 5–7 days after stopping fluoxetine before starting mirtazapine at 15 mg nocte. Titrate cautiously. The main serotonin syndrome risk is low between these two agents (mirtazapine is not primarily serotonergic), but the CYP interaction is the primary concern.

rules.headline: Direct switch possible — taper mirtazapine and start fluoxetine
rules.detail: Stop mirtazapine and start fluoxetine 20 mg the next day. There is no significant pharmacokinetic interaction in this direction: fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 but mirtazapine is being stopped (not started). The main clinical issue is the loss of mirtazapine's sedating antihistaminergic effect — warn the patient about potential rebound insomnia during the transition. Fluoxetine takes 4–6 weeks to reach full effect; brief antidepressant discontinuation symptoms from mirtazapine are possible. A brief cross-taper overlapping both drugs by 1 week is also acceptable if the transition needs to be gentler.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — fluvoxamine's CYP inhibition resolves as dose falls
rules.detail: Fluvoxamine is a potent CYP1A2 and CYP2C19 inhibitor (and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor). As the fluvoxamine dose is tapered down, these enzyme inhibitions resolve, which may affect plasma levels of any co-prescribed drugs that are CYP1A2/2C19 substrates. During the cross-taper, introduce the new SSRI at a standard starting dose while reducing fluvoxamine gradually over 1–2 weeks. Watch for serotonergic overlap symptoms (tremor, myoclonus, agitation). Review all co-medications for CYP1A2/2C19 substrate interactions before and after the switch.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — introducing fluvoxamine adds potent CYP1A2/2C19 inhibition
rules.detail: When starting fluvoxamine, its potent CYP1A2 and CYP2C19 inhibition begins to develop within days of dosing. Any co-prescribed drugs that are CYP1A2/2C19/3A4 substrates (e.g. clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline, warfarin, omeprazole) will have their plasma levels rise — review and adjust doses of affected drugs before starting fluvoxamine. Cross-taper over 1–2 weeks. Watch for serotonergic symptoms during overlap. Fluvoxamine also inhibits agomelatine metabolism (CYP1A2) — co-prescription with agomelatine is contraindicated and must be stopped before fluvoxamine is introduced.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — fluvoxamine inhibits venlafaxine/duloxetine metabolism via CYP2C19
rules.detail: Fluvoxamine inhibits CYP2C19 (and to a lesser extent CYP2D6 and CYP3A4), relevant to SNRI metabolism. Venlafaxine is a CYP2C19 substrate — if venlafaxine is introduced while fluvoxamine inhibition is still present, venlafaxine levels may be higher than expected. Reduce fluvoxamine gradually over 1–2 weeks while introducing the SNRI at a low starting dose. Additive serotonergic and noradrenergic effects are possible during overlap. Venlafaxine discontinuation syndrome risk is also relevant as the SNRI is being introduced — titrate the SNRI upwards once fluvoxamine is fully stopped.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — introducing fluvoxamine raises SNRI levels via CYP inhibition
rules.detail: Fluvoxamine inhibits CYP2C19 which metabolizes venlafaxine — starting fluvoxamine while the SNRI is still being tapered will inhibit SNRI clearance and raise SNRI plasma levels unexpectedly. Introduce fluvoxamine at a low dose (50 mg) once the SNRI is at its lowest step, then taper and stop the SNRI. Additive serotonergic effects during overlap. SNRI discontinuation syndrome (particularly venlafaxine) is a key risk — consider hyperbolic taper for venlafaxine. Review all co-medications for new CYP1A2/2C19 substrate interactions once fluvoxamine is established.

rules.headline: Taper and stop fluvoxamine, wait 7 days for CYP1A2 recovery, then start mirtazapine at low dose
rules.detail: Fluvoxamine is a potent CYP1A2 inhibitor, and mirtazapine is a primary CYP1A2 substrate. Co-prescribing fluvoxamine with mirtazapine dramatically raises mirtazapine levels — this combination is clinically hazardous. When transitioning to mirtazapine, taper and stop fluvoxamine completely, then wait approximately 7 days for CYP1A2 activity to recover before starting mirtazapine. Start mirtazapine at 15 mg nocte (low dose, not the usual starting dose) and titrate cautiously once CYP1A2 inhibition is resolved. Starting mirtazapine before fluvoxamine has fully cleared risks severe sedation, hypotension, and toxicity from supra-therapeutic mirtazapine exposure.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — as fluvoxamine titrates up, it inhibits CYP1A2 and raises mirtazapine levels
rules.detail: When starting fluvoxamine while tapering mirtazapine, be aware that fluvoxamine's rising CYP1A2 inhibition will progressively increase mirtazapine plasma levels — even as the mirtazapine dose is reduced, levels may not fall as expected. Ensure mirtazapine is tapered briskly once fluvoxamine has been introduced (do not let both be at full dose simultaneously). Mirtazapine should ideally be stopped before fluvoxamine is titrated above 100 mg. Monitor for excessive sedation during the overlap period. Loss of mirtazapine's antihistaminergic sedation may cause rebound insomnia.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — both drugs are high-inhibitor SSRIs; prolonged serotonergic overlap expected
rules.detail: Both fluvoxamine and fluoxetine are potent CYP inhibitors with different enzyme targets (fluvoxamine: CYP1A2/2C19/3A4; fluoxetine: CYP2D6/2C9). Cross-tapering introduces additive serotonin syndrome risk and complex bidirectional CYP interactions. Fluvoxamine inhibits CYP2C9 which metabolizes fluoxetine — as fluvoxamine is tapered, fluoxetine clearance increases and levels may fall. Introduce fluoxetine at a low dose (10–20 mg) while reducing fluvoxamine over 1–2 weeks. Note that fluoxetine's long half-life (plus norfluoxetine) means effective levels persist for 5–6 weeks after the last dose — once established, fluoxetine provides a long 'bridge'. CYP inhibition patterns shift during the transition; review all co-medications.

rules.headline: Stop fluoxetine, wait 5–7 days, then start fluvoxamine — allow full washout before titrating fluvoxamine
rules.detail: Fluoxetine (and norfluoxetine) inhibits CYP2D6, which is involved in fluvoxamine metabolism. Starting fluvoxamine while fluoxetine's CYP2D6 inhibition is still active risks elevated fluvoxamine levels and unpredictable CYP1A2/2C19 inhibition onset. After stopping fluoxetine, allow 5–7 days before starting fluvoxamine at its standard starting dose (50 mg). Note that norfluoxetine has a 7–9 day half-life — full CYP2D6 recovery takes several weeks, so fluvoxamine titration should proceed cautiously over the first month. Review all CYP1A2/2C19 substrate co-medications before introducing fluvoxamine.

rules.headline: Taper and stop fluvoxamine, wait 7 days for CYP inhibition to resolve, then start vortioxetine at half dose
rules.detail: Fluvoxamine inhibits multiple CYP enzymes involved in vortioxetine metabolism (CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP3A4). Starting vortioxetine while fluvoxamine's CYP inhibition is still present will result in significantly elevated vortioxetine plasma levels. Taper and stop fluvoxamine, then wait 7 days before starting vortioxetine at 5 mg (half the standard 10 mg starting dose). Titrate cautiously over the following 2–3 weeks. The serotonergic overlap risk (from residual fluvoxamine) combined with elevated vortioxetine levels could precipitate serotonin syndrome if the transition is rushed.

rules.headline: Cross-taper cautiously — as fluvoxamine titrates up it inhibits CYP enzymes metabolising vortioxetine
rules.detail: When fluvoxamine is introduced while vortioxetine is being tapered, rising fluvoxamine-mediated CYP2C9/2C19 inhibition will raise vortioxetine plasma levels — even as the vortioxetine dose is reduced, levels may remain unexpectedly high. Ensure vortioxetine is tapered briskly once fluvoxamine has been started. Vortioxetine's long half-life (~66 h) means serotonergic activity declines slowly. Monitor for additive serotonergic symptoms (tremor, agitation, myoclonus) during the overlap. Review all CYP1A2/2C19 substrate co-medications before fluvoxamine is fully titrated.

rules.headline: Taper and stop fluvoxamine, wait 14 days, then start moclobemide
rules.detail: Fluvoxamine is a serotonergic agent — despite moclobemide's reversibility, a 14-day washout from any serotonergic drug is required before starting moclobemide to avoid serotonin syndrome. Additionally, fluvoxamine inhibits CYP1A2 which metabolizes moclobemide — waiting 14 days also allows the CYP1A2 inhibition from fluvoxamine to fully resolve before moclobemide is introduced. Taper fluvoxamine to zero before starting the washout period.

rules.headline: Stop moclobemide, wait 24 hours, then start fluvoxamine
rules.detail: Moclobemide is a reversible MAOI; its MAO-A inhibition resolves within 24 hours of stopping. After this short washout, fluvoxamine can be safely started at its standard dose (50 mg once daily). Note: once fluvoxamine is established, it inhibits CYP1A2 which metabolizes moclobemide — if moclobemide is ever reintroduced, the dose would need to be reduced. Counsel the patient accordingly.

qtc.rationale: QTc prolongation causes Torsades de Pointes (TdP), a potentially fatal ventricular arrhythmia. Multiple QTc-prolonging drugs used together have additive (and sometimes synergistic) effects. This registry uses CredibleMeds / AzCERT risk categories adapted for the Malaysian formulary. Individual QTc risk increases with: older age, female sex, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, bradycardia, heart failure, hepatic impairment, and genetic predisposition. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW — Rashid Razak.

riskCategories.known: Known Risk of TdP — substantial evidence for QTc prolongation and TdP. Avoid with other QTc-prolonging drugs unless closely monitored.
riskCategories.conditional: Conditional Risk of TdP — evidence for QTc prolongation; TdP risk increases under certain conditions (e.g. high dose, hypokalaemia, rapid IV infusion, drug interaction).
riskCategories.possible: Possible Risk of TdP — evidence for QTc prolongation but insufficient data to determine TdP risk.
riskCategories.low: Low / Negligible Risk — limited or no evidence for clinically significant QTc effect.

drugs.name: Haloperidol
drugs.notes: Risk substantially higher with IV route and doses > 35 mg/day. Oral haloperidol at standard doses is conditional risk in most classifications but well-established QTc prolonger.

drugs.name: Clozapine
drugs.notes: QTc prolongation documented at higher doses. Risk increased by rapid titration, metabolic syndrome, or combined with other QTc drugs.

drugs.name: Quetiapine
drugs.notes: Dose-dependent QTc effect. Most risk at higher doses (> 600 mg/day) or in overdose. Particularly risky in combination with other QTc-prolonging drugs.

drugs.name: Risperidone
drugs.notes: Moderate QTc prolongation. Risk increased at higher doses and in elderly patients.

drugs.name: Olanzapine
drugs.notes: Modest QTc effect. Less concerning than haloperidol or quetiapine at standard doses.

drugs.name: Aripiprazole
drugs.notes: Minimal QTc effect — one of the lowest-risk antipsychotics. Some case reports of QTc prolongation at very high doses.

drugs.name: Escitalopram
drugs.notes: Dose-dependent QTc prolongation. Maximum dose in cardiac patients is 10 mg/day (elderly) or 20 mg/day (adults). MHRA restriction in 2011. Avoid with other QTc-prolonging drugs.

drugs.name: Citalopram
drugs.notes: Similar QTc effect to escitalopram. Maximum dose in cardiac patients or elderly is reduced. Not currently in the PsychSwitch switching registry.

drugs.name: Sertraline
drugs.notes: Mild QTc prolongation at therapeutic doses. Generally considered safer than escitalopram for cardiac patients.

drugs.name: Fluoxetine
drugs.notes: CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 inhibition can raise levels of co-prescribed QTc-prolonging drugs — the drug interaction risk may exceed the direct QTc risk.

drugs.name: Venlafaxine
drugs.notes: QTc prolongation at higher doses (> 225 mg/day). Lower risk at standard doses.

drugs.name: Paroxetine
drugs.notes: Weak QTc effect. CYP2D6 inhibition raises levels of co-prescribed drugs.

drugs.name: Mirtazapine
drugs.notes: Mild QTc prolongation reported in overdose and at high doses. Generally considered low risk at therapeutic doses.

drugs.name: Lithium
drugs.notes: QTc prolongation documented at toxic levels. At therapeutic levels the effect is minimal, but caution in patients with cardiac disease.

drugs.name: Lamotrigine
drugs.notes: No clinically significant QTc effect at therapeutic doses.

drugs.name: Sodium valproate
drugs.notes: No clinically significant QTc effect.

drugs.name: Carbamazepine
drugs.notes: Sodium channel blocker — can cause PR and QRS prolongation but minimal effect on QTc.

drugs.name: Methadone
drugs.notes: High risk — one of the most potent QTc-prolonging drugs in clinical use. Requires baseline and periodic ECG. Avoid combining with other QTc-prolonging drugs.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.notes: Common antibiotic with well-documented QTc-prolonging effect. Commonly co-prescribed — always check for QTc-prolonging psychiatric medications.

drugs.name: Erythromycin
drugs.notes: Higher risk than azithromycin. Also a CYP3A4 inhibitor — may raise levels of co-prescribed antipsychotics.

drugs.name: Domperidone
drugs.notes: Common antiemetic — frequently prescribed without recognition of QTc risk. Avoid with antipsychotics.

drugs.name: Ondansetron
drugs.notes: Particularly relevant in inpatient psychiatry where antiemetics are commonly used. IV route has higher QTc risk than oral.

drugs.name: Amitriptyline
drugs.notes: TCA with sodium channel blockade and QTc prolongation. Not in the switching registry (TCA) but commonly co-prescribed for pain or sleep.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.notes: Fluoroquinolone with QTc prolongation. CYP1A2 inhibitor — significantly raises clozapine and olanzapine levels. Double interaction risk.

riskThresholds.overallAssessmentNote: Risk is additive. Any combination of 'known' + 'conditional' risk drugs warrants baseline ECG and monitoring. Two or more 'known' risk drugs together is a high-risk combination — seek cardiology input if QTc > 480 ms (men) or > 500 ms (women).

lithium-tapering.title: Stopping lithium
lithium-tapering.rationale: Per Maudsley 15th edition (Bipolar disorder chapter, pp.331–333). Stopping lithium carries a substantial risk of mood relapse — particularly manic rebound. Time to a new mood episode after lithium discontinuation is approximately 1.7 months on average, vs ~11.6 months between episodes in untreated bipolar disorder: a sevenfold increase in relapse rate. Most of this excess relapse is concentrated in the first 3 months post-discontinuation. Lithium should NOT be stopped abruptly unless a serious adverse effect demands it. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW — Rashid Razak.
whenToConsiderStopping: Patient request after informed discussion of relapse risk
Tolerability problems: diarrhoea (~13%), tremor (~11%), polyuria/polydipsia/diabetes insipidus (~9%), creatinine rise (~9%), weight gain (~7%)
Significant adverse effects: thyroid dysfunction, persistent renal impairment, neurotoxicity
Pregnancy planning (Ebstein's anomaly risk in first trimester — discuss specialist switch)
Long-term remission with prescriber agreement that taper trial is justified

withdrawalEffects.rationale: Withdrawal effects are thought to result from dopaminergic hypersensitivity and changes in neuronal membranes that develop during long-term lithium treatment. They may be misinterpreted as relapse — extending the withdrawal period helps distinguish withdrawal-related rebound from true relapse.

tapering.principle: Hyperbolic tapering — reduce by the same percentage of the CURRENT dose each step, so that the absolute reduction becomes smaller and smaller as the total dose decreases. This mitigates abrupt receptor occupancy changes which underlie withdrawal symptoms.
tapering.rapidVsGradual: Rapid (1–14 day) discontinuation produces substantially higher relapse rates than gradual (15–30 day) tapering. NICE recommends a minimum 4-week to 5-month taper. Some evidence suggests even 2–5 month tapering yields higher relapse than continuation, supporting an even slower taper where possible.
tapering.initialReduction: 10–25% reduction of the current dose, with monitoring of withdrawal and mood symptoms for at least 4 weeks before further reduction.
tapering.minimumDoseBeforeStop: Final pre-stop dose may be very small — e.g. ~1% of therapeutic dose (around 10 mg for lithium) — because small doses have disproportionately large effects on target receptors. Compounded capsules from specialist pharmacy may be needed in some settings.

maudsleyRegimen.title: Suggested slow reduction regimen for lithium (Maudsley 15, Box 2.3)

steps.notes: Reduce by 200 mg each month until total daily dose reaches 800 mg.
Reduce by 100 mg each month until 400 mg/day.
Reduce by 50 mg each month until 200 mg/day.
Reduce by 25 mg each month until completely stopped.

maudsleyRegimen.totalDurationNote: From a typical maintenance dose of around 1000 mg/day, this regimen takes roughly 12 months to reach zero. A slower regimen is acceptable and often preferable; a faster regimen is appropriate only if a serious adverse effect mandates earlier discontinuation.

monitoringDuringTaper: Mood state (PHQ-9 / mood diary at minimum, plus clinical review)
Withdrawal symptoms (physical and psychological, see table)
Lithium level (every 1–2 months during taper, since clearance is unchanged but compliance is checked)
Renal function (U&E, eGFR) and TFTs at baseline and 3-monthly
Pause or reverse the taper if early manic features (sleep changes, increased energy, racing thoughts) emerge
ifSymptomsEmerge: Pause the current dose and observe — many withdrawal effects resolve within 2–4 weeks
Slow the taper — extend the interval between steps, or reduce step size
Revert to the previously effective dose if relapse is confirmed
Difficulty reducing does NOT preclude future attempts — it usually indicates a more gradual schedule is needed
Consider adjunctive psychotherapy, psychoeducation, or social rhythm therapy throughout the tapering period
neverDoThis: Stop lithium abruptly unless a serious adverse effect (lithium toxicity, severe rash, NMS) demands it — abrupt cessation has produced manic episodes in up to 13% of patients in some studies
Skip mood monitoring during the taper — early signs of mood elevation are the warning sign
Confuse withdrawal-induced symptoms with true relapse during the first 4–8 weeks of tapering — extend the taper to clarify
lithium-tapering.otherMoodStabilizers: Withdrawal effects are also documented for valproate, lamotrigine and carbamazepine, although evidence is less robust than for lithium. The same hyperbolic taper principle and slow timeline apply: reduce by 10–25% of current dose, monitor for ≥4 weeks at each step, and continue indefinitely until zero or until destabilisation halts the process. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

titration-female-non-smoker.rationale: Per Maudsley 15th edition (Schizophrenia chapter, p.216–217). Female non-smokers have the lowest CYP1A2-mediated clozapine clearance, so the target maintenance dose is 225 mg/day — the lowest of the four pharmacokinetic variants. The schedule is gentle: 6.25 mg evening for the first two days, slow build-up over 20 days. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

steps.notes: First test dose 6.25 mg evening. Lying and standing BP at 1, 2 and 4 hours post-dose. Pulse and temperature 4-hourly.
Continue 6.25 mg evening only. Repeat lying/standing BP morning, post-dose × 3.
Begin BD dosing. BP monitoring continues.
Watch for postural drop. Counsel about hypersalivation and constipation.
Start prophylactic laxative if not already (constipation is universal).
Watch for sedation, weight gain trajectory.
Reassess myocarditis warning signs (chest pain, palpitations, fever, dyspnoea).
Hold and reassess if any concerns.
Maintenance target reached. Continue with weekly FBC, troponin/CRP at weeks 2 and 4.

titration-female-non-smoker.postTitrationGuidance: Maintain at 225 mg/day. Plasma level optimisation may follow once stable (target 350–600 ng/mL). Weekly FBC for first 18 weeks, then fortnightly for weeks 19–52, then monthly indefinitely. Faster titrations may be appropriate in younger patients without prominent dose-related side effects, particularly when cross-tapering from a previous antipsychotic.
titration-female-non-smoker.missedDoseRule: Doses missed for more than 48 hours mandate retitration. Use the Interruption Restart Wizard for the appropriate restart strategy. Restarting at the previous dose after a gap can cause severe hypotension and cardiovascular collapse.

titration-female-smoker.rationale: Per Maudsley 15th edition (Schizophrenia chapter, p.216–217). Smoking induces CYP1A2, accelerating clozapine clearance. Female smokers therefore need a higher target maintenance dose (300 mg/day) than female non-smokers (225 mg/day). If the patient stops smoking during or after titration, clozapine levels can rise sharply — measure plasma level and reduce dose if necessary. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

steps.notes: First test dose 6.25 mg evening. Lying and standing BP at 1, 2 and 4 hours post-dose.
Counsel about hypersalivation and constipation. Start prophylactic laxative.
Hold a day if tolerability concerns.
Maintenance target reached. If patient stops smoking, plasma levels can rise sharply — recheck level and consider dose reduction.

titration-female-smoker.postTitrationGuidance: Maintain at 300 mg/day. Smoking cessation post-titration can substantially raise clozapine levels — monitor plasma levels closely and reduce dose proportionally if needed. Faster titration may be appropriate in younger patients without prominent dose-related side effects.
titration-female-smoker.missedDoseRule: Doses missed for more than 48 hours mandate retitration. Use the Interruption Restart Wizard.

titration-male-non-smoker.rationale: Per Maudsley 15th edition (Schizophrenia chapter, p.217). Male non-smokers have moderate CYP1A2 activity — between female non-smokers (225 mg target) and male smokers (375 mg target). Target maintenance dose: 250 mg/day. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

steps.notes: First test dose 6.25 mg evening. Lying and standing BP at 1, 2 and 4 hours post-dose. Pulse and temperature 4-hourly.
Continue 6.25 mg evening only. BP monitoring continues.
Watch for postural drop. Counsel about hypersalivation and constipation.
Maintenance target reached. Plasma level optimisation may follow once stable.

titration-male-non-smoker.postTitrationGuidance: Maintain at 250 mg/day. Plasma level optimisation may follow once stable (target 350–600 ng/mL). Faster titration may be appropriate in younger patients without prominent side effects, particularly when cross-tapering from a previous antipsychotic.
titration-male-non-smoker.missedDoseRule: Doses missed for more than 48 hours mandate retitration. Use the Interruption Restart Wizard.

titration-male-smoker.rationale: Per Maudsley 15th edition (Schizophrenia chapter, p.218). Male smokers have the highest CYP1A2 activity, requiring the highest maintenance target (375 mg/day) to achieve therapeutic plasma levels. Smoking induction must be considered: if the patient stops smoking during clozapine treatment, plasma levels can DOUBLE within 4 weeks — recheck level and reduce dose accordingly. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

steps.notes: First test dose 6.25 mg evening. Lying and standing BP at 1, 2 and 4 hours post-dose.
Counsel about hypersalivation, constipation. Start prophylactic laxative.
Hold a day if tolerability concerns.
Maintenance target reached. Critical: if patient stops smoking, plasma levels can rise sharply (up to 2× within 4 weeks). Check plasma level and reduce dose if needed.

titration-male-smoker.postTitrationGuidance: Maintain at 375 mg/day. CRITICAL — smoking cessation post-titration: clozapine plasma levels can rise by up to 2× within 4 weeks. Recheck plasma level on smoking cessation and reduce dose accordingly. Plasma level optimisation target 350–600 ng/mL.
titration-male-smoker.missedDoseRule: Doses missed for more than 48 hours mandate retitration. Use the Interruption Restart Wizard.

monitoring-schedule.rationale: Mandatory monitoring schedule based on Maudsley 14th edition, Novartis Clozaril SmPC and the UK CPMS / Malaysian clozapine monitoring service standards. Failure to monitor is a recognised cause of clozapine-related agranulocytosis death. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

phases.notes: Mandatory weekly haematological monitoring for the first 18 weeks. Highest agranulocytosis risk window.
Reduced frequency from week 19 to end of year 1, provided counts remain in green range.
Indefinite monthly FBC + ANC for as long as clozapine is prescribed. NO ceiling — monitoring continues lifelong.

milestones.criticalNotes: Confirm registration on local clozapine monitoring service before first dose. Confirm ANC ≥2.0 × 10⁹/L and WBC ≥3.5 × 10⁹/L (or BEN-adjusted thresholds). Document pregnancy status if applicable.
Myocarditis risk window opens. Low threshold for troponin + CRP if any of: fever, persistent tachycardia (HR >100), chest pain, dyspnoea, fatigue, flu-like symptoms.
Myocarditis risk peak. Continue cardiac vigilance. Some centres routinely repeat troponin + CRP at this milestone.
First scheduled metabolic and cardiac re-screen. Plasma clozapine level — aim 350-600 ng/mL (clozapine), interpret with norclozapine.
Comprehensive annual review. Document continued indication, tolerability and response. Frequency of FBC + ANC drops to monthly from now on.
Repeat the comprehensive panel each year. Continue MONTHLY FBC + ANC indefinitely.

actions.amber: Continue clozapine but increase FBC + ANC to twice weekly until counts stabilise in green or fall to red.
actions.red: STOP clozapine immediately. Daily FBC + ANC. Refer to haematology. Do NOT re-challenge without specialist review and clozapine monitoring service approval.

benAdjustment.notes: BEN-adjusted thresholds for documented Benign Ethnic Neutropenia (relevant for some Malaysian, African, Middle Eastern and South Asian patients). Confirm BEN diagnosis with haematology before applying. Cutoffs follow Maudsley / CPMS-UK guidance; precise numbers vary slightly by reference. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

considerations.title: Agranulocytosis / severe neutropenia
considerations.body: Lifetime cumulative incidence ~0.8%. Highest risk weeks 6-18, but can occur at any time. Mandatory FBC + ANC monitoring per schedule. ANC <1.5 × 10⁹/L: STOP clozapine immediately, daily FBCs, refer haematology. Do NOT re-challenge without specialist review.
considerations.monitoring: FBC + ANC weekly weeks 1-18, fortnightly weeks 19-52, monthly thereafter — for life.

considerations.title: Clozapine-induced myocarditis
considerations.body: Peak risk weeks 2-4. Australian rates suggest ~1% of initiations. Red flags: fever, persistent tachycardia (HR consistently >100), chest pain, dyspnoea, flu-like symptoms in the first 6 weeks. Investigate immediately with troponin + CRP + ECG. Echocardiography if abnormal.
considerations.monitoring: Baseline troponin, CRP, ECG. Repeat if symptomatic. Some centres repeat routinely at week 2-4.

considerations.title: Constipation and paralytic ileus
considerations.body: Clozapine has potent M3 antagonism, slowing GI motility. Paralytic ileus is a leading cause of clozapine-related death — more lives lost than agranulocytosis in some series. Universal prophylactic laxatives. Document bowel function daily during inpatient titration and at every clinic visit thereafter. Any patient reporting no bowel motion >3 days requires urgent review.
considerations.monitoring: Bowel chart during titration. Stool softener + stimulant laxative routinely (e.g. docusate + senna). Investigate any abdominal pain or distension promptly.

considerations.title: Seizures (dose-dependent)
considerations.body: Risk rises sharply above 600 mg/day. Myoclonic jerks and drop attacks may precede generalised seizures. EEG and prophylactic anticonvulsant (sodium valproate typical) consideration above 600 mg/day or in patients with prior seizure history.
considerations.monitoring: Clinical monitoring during titration. EEG if dose ≥600 mg or if myoclonus, drop attacks, or seizure-like activity reported.

considerations.title: Smoking — sudden cessation can DOUBLE clozapine levels
considerations.body: Tobacco smoking is a potent CYP1A2 inducer. Patients stable on clozapine who suddenly stop smoking (e.g. on hospital admission, NRT initiation) can see plasma levels double within 1-2 weeks, with risk of toxicity, sedation and seizures. Counsel every smoker on stable clozapine at every visit. Reduce dose proactively if planned cessation; recheck plasma levels after 1-2 weeks.
considerations.monitoring: Document smoking status at every clinic visit. Plasma level 1-2 weeks after any change in smoking habits.

considerations.title: Hypersalivation
considerations.body: Almost universal, paradoxical despite clozapine's strong anticholinergic profile (M4 partial agonism is implicated). Typically nocturnal. Manage with positioning (towel on pillow) first. Pharmacological options (hyoscine, glycopyrrolate, atropine drops sublingually) only if severe and bothersome.
considerations.monitoring: Ask at every visit. Severe hypersalivation can compromise sleep and adherence.

considerations.title: Weight gain, glucose dysregulation, dyslipidaemia
considerations.body: Among the worst antipsychotics for metabolic burden. New-onset type 2 diabetes can occur even without weight gain. Mandatory metabolic monitoring at baseline, 3 months, 6 months, then annually. Lifestyle counseling at every visit; consider metformin co-prescription for weight gain.
considerations.monitoring: Weight, BMI, waist, BP, fasting glucose / HbA1c, lipid profile per the milestone schedule.

considerations.title: Orthostatic hypotension during titration
considerations.body: Most pronounced in first 2 weeks. Slow titration, lying-and-standing BP at every visit during titration, fall precautions. Severe orthostasis warrants slowing the titration or, rarely, halting and re-challenging at lower doses.
considerations.monitoring: Lying and standing BP and pulse at every titration step.

considerations.title: Re-titration after interruption ≥48 hours
considerations.body: Tolerance to orthostasis and sedation is lost rapidly. ANY interruption of 48 hours or more mandates re-titration starting at 12.5 mg, regardless of how high the previous maintenance dose was. This is non-negotiable. Re-titration follows the inpatient or community schedule depending on setting.
considerations.monitoring: Confirm continuous dosing at every clinic visit. Re-start protocol if any doubt.

rechallenge-rules.rationale: Per Maudsley 15th edition (Schizophrenia chapter, p.234 'Restarting clozapine after a break in treatment'): clozapine tolerance to cardiovascular and sedative effects is lost rapidly on interruption. Restarting at the previously tolerated dose after a gap of more than 48 hours can cause severe hypotension, cardiovascular collapse, and has been associated with deaths. The risk is reduced — but not eliminated — in patients who have been on clozapine in the recent past, especially for an extended period. Hypotension is more frequent if clozapine is reintroduced more rapidly than the original dose was reached. The required restart strategy depends on the duration of interruption. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW — Rashid Razak.

tiers.label: < 24 hours
tiers.heading: Continue at current dose
tiers.guidance: A gap of fewer than 24 hours does not require dose reduction. Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, then continue the regular schedule. If the next scheduled dose is within 6 hours, skip the missed dose and resume normally.
tiers.monitoringNote: Standard monitoring. No additional observations required unless symptomatic.

tiers.label: 24 – 48 hours
tiers.heading: Halve the dose for 48 hours, then retitrate
tiers.guidance: After 24–48 h without clozapine, significant tolerance loss begins. Restart at half the usual dose for 2 days with BP and pulse monitoring at 1 h and 2 h post-dose, then return to the previous maintenance dose if tolerated.
tiers.restartInstruction: Restart at 50% of the last maintenance dose. Increase back to full dose after 48 h if tolerated.
tiers.monitoringNote: BP and HR at 1 h and 2 h after first restarted dose. Observe for postural hypotension.

tiers.label: 2 – 5 days
tiers.heading: Restart at 25 mg and retitrate over 1–2 weeks
tiers.guidance: After 2–5 days off clozapine, restart from 25 mg nocte (NOT the previous dose — doing so risks severe cardiovascular collapse). Follow an accelerated inpatient retitration schedule, reaching the target maintenance dose over 7–14 days. Inpatient setting strongly preferred for the first 3–4 days.
tiers.restartInstruction: Restart at 25 mg nocte. Increase by 25 mg every 1–2 days as tolerated. BP monitoring required.
tiers.monitoringNote: BP and HR at 1 h and 2 h post-dose for the first 3–5 days. Restart FBC monitoring from the start of the retitration schedule.

tiers.label: > 5 days
tiers.heading: Full retitration from 12.5 mg — treat as new initiation
tiers.guidance: After more than 5 days off clozapine, full tolerance to cardiovascular and sedative effects is lost. Restart must follow the full initiation protocol (12.5 mg on day 1, inpatient titration preferred) regardless of the previous stable dose. Restarting at the prior maintenance dose at this stage has caused deaths.
tiers.restartInstruction: Restart using the standard inpatient titration protocol from 12.5 mg. Target the previous maintenance dose only after the full titration schedule is complete.
tiers.monitoringNote: Full inpatient monitoring for at least the first 14 days. FBC monitoring restarts from week 1 (weekly for first 18 weeks). Reconsider if prior agranulocytosis — rechallenge generally contraindicated.
warningSignsToWatch: myocarditis symptoms (chest pain, palpitations, fever, dyspnoea)

absoluteContraindications: Previous clozapine-induced agranulocytosis (ANC < 0.5 ×10⁹/L) — rechallenge contraindicated in most jurisdictions.
Previous clozapine-induced myocarditis — rechallenge only under specialist cardiology and psychiatry co-management.
citations: Clozaril (clozapine) Summary of Product Characteristics. Novartis.
Barnes TR et al. Evidence-based guidelines for the pharmacological treatment of schizophrenia. J Psychopharmacol. 2020.

community-initiation.rationale: Per Maudsley 15th edition (Schizophrenia chapter, p.236). Although clozapine initiation is most commonly performed in inpatient settings, community initiation is feasible for selected patients with appropriate adherence, support, and monitoring infrastructure. The titration schedule itself is no different — it is the SUITABILITY criteria, monitoring intensity, and contingency planning that differ. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

relativeContraindications.title: Uncontrolled seizure disorder
relativeContraindications.detail: Clozapine lowers the seizure threshold dose-dependently. Active or poorly-controlled epilepsy is a strong contraindication to community initiation.

relativeContraindications.title: Significant cardiac disease
relativeContraindications.detail: Includes ischaemic heart disease, prior myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, severe hypertension, or unstable arrhythmia. Cardiac complications during titration may not be safely managed in the community.

relativeContraindications.title: Unstable diabetes
relativeContraindications.detail: Clozapine causes metabolic dysregulation and can precipitate diabetic ketoacidosis. Glucose stability needs to be confirmed before community initiation.

relativeContraindications.title: History of paralytic ileus or severe constipation
relativeContraindications.detail: Clozapine-induced gastrointestinal hypomotility can be life-threatening. Pre-existing motility disorders disqualify community initiation.

relativeContraindications.title: Significant blood dyscrasia
relativeContraindications.detail: Pre-existing neutropenia, agranulocytosis history, or other haematological disorder. Discuss with haematology before any clozapine.

relativeContraindications.title: Previous severe adverse effect on AP titration
relativeContraindications.detail: Severe orthostasis, sedation, NMS, or other significant adverse event on a previous antipsychotic introduction predicts higher risk on clozapine.

relativeContraindications.title: Unreliable or chaotic lifestyle
relativeContraindications.detail: Patient must be able to attend monitoring appointments and follow the titration schedule reliably. Homelessness, severe substance use disorder, or poor medication adherence pattern disqualifies community initiation.

relativeContraindications.title: Significant alcohol or stimulant misuse
relativeContraindications.detail: Cocaine, methamphetamine, or heavy alcohol use markedly increases the risk of cardiotoxicity, seizures, and adherence failure. Address substance use before community initiation.

essentialCriteria.title: Patient likely to be adherent
essentialCriteria.detail: Both with the medication itself AND with the monitoring requirements. Honest discussion with patient and family — clozapine is a lifelong commitment with rigid blood-test rhythms.

essentialCriteria.title: Adequate support network
essentialCriteria.detail: Family member, carer, or supported-living staff who can recognise warning signs (orthostatic dizziness, fever, chest pain, severe sedation) and seek help if the patient cannot.

essentialCriteria.title: Patient understands monitoring requirements
essentialCriteria.detail: Has been counselled about the regular blood tests, ECGs, and physical-health checks. Understands clozapine cannot continue without them.

essentialCriteria.title: Patient understands possible adverse effects
essentialCriteria.detail: Particularly the rare but serious ones: agranulocytosis (any unexplained infection or fever → urgent FBC), myocarditis (chest pain, palpitations, dyspnoea, fever in first 8 weeks), constipation/ileus.

essentialCriteria.title: Patient readily contactable
essentialCriteria.detail: Phone number, address, or other reliable contact method. Critical for following up abnormal results and communicating dose changes.

essentialCriteria.title: Can be reviewed weekly during titration
essentialCriteria.detail: Either by physical attendance at clinic, home visit, or telehealth. The first 18 weeks of clozapine require weekly FBC AND clinical review.

essentialCriteria.title: Reliable medication supply
essentialCriteria.detail: Patient can collect weekly clozapine OR medication can be delivered. Pharmacy-coordinated supply is often the most reliable approach.

essentialCriteria.title: Can access help out-of-hours
essentialCriteria.detail: Patient knows what to do if they develop fever, chest pain, severe sedation, or any red-flag symptom. Has an out-of-hours number and understands when to use the emergency department.

essentialCriteria.title: Understands action on abnormal blood results
essentialCriteria.detail: If a RED result occurs, daily monitoring of FBC until normalisation. Patient must understand the urgency and not miss any of these intensive follow-up tests.

initialWorkup.title: Physical examination
initialWorkup.detail: Including baseline weight, BP, pulse, temperature, and abdominal exam (bowel sounds, organomegaly).

initialWorkup.title: Full blood count with differential
initialWorkup.detail: Mandatory baseline. Any patient with low-baseline neutrophils — investigate for benign ethnic neutropenia (BEN) before disqualifying.

initialWorkup.title: Liver function tests
initialWorkup.detail: Including ALT. Required at baseline; clozapine can cause hepatic dysfunction.

initialWorkup.title: Urea & electrolytes, creatinine
initialWorkup.detail: Renal function affects metabolite clearance and is required before initiation.

initialWorkup.title: Lipid profile, fasting glucose / HbA1c
initialWorkup.detail: Baseline metabolic profile. Clozapine causes substantial metabolic disturbance — establish a starting point before the inevitable shifts.

initialWorkup.title: CRP and troponin
initialWorkup.detail: Baseline cardiac biomarkers. Will be repeated weekly for the first 4 weeks to screen for clozapine-induced myocarditis (peak risk weeks 1–4).

initialWorkup.title: ECG
initialWorkup.detail: Baseline 12-lead ECG. Specifically screen for evidence of past myocardial infarction, ventricular hypertrophy, or QTc prolongation.

initialWorkup.title: Echocardiogram (if clinically indicated)
initialWorkup.detail: For patients with ECG abnormality, prior cardiac history, or risk factors for cardiomyopathy.

initialWorkup.title: BEN workup if low baseline ANC
initialWorkup.detail: If baseline neutrophils are low, consider benign ethnic neutropenia (common in patients of African, Middle Eastern, or some Asian backgrounds). Genetic testing for the DARC variant available; serial counts also helpful.

initialWorkup.title: Inform the patient's GP
initialWorkup.detail: Critical — the GP needs to be aware of the clozapine treatment and monitoring schedule, especially for inter-current illness management (any febrile illness should trigger an urgent FBC).

monitoringIntensity.first_4_weeks: Weekly FBC + weekly CRP + weekly troponin + clinical review (BP, pulse, temperature, side-effect screen, bowel function).
monitoringIntensity.weeks_5_to_18: Weekly FBC + clinical review. CRP/troponin only if symptomatic.
monitoringIntensity.year_2_onwards: Monthly FBC + 6-monthly metabolic monitoring + annual cardiometabolic review.
